checklist.step: Scope the PMIERs financial-reporting control universe for the quarter
actions: Pull the mortgage guaranty trial balance from SAP S/4HANA ▸ Financial Accounting ▸ Reporting and list every account that feeds Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets, unearned premium and loss reserves.

In AuditBoard open the SOXHUB scoping module and create the PMIERs cycle with sub-processes: Available Assets, MRA / Exhibit A factors, Exhibit F loan-level dataset, premium and reserve close, and Section 304 segregation.
Ask the Head of Capital Management for the prior-quarter PMIERs sufficiency ratio and the dollar cushion of Available Assets over MRA so scoping targets the accounts that move the ratio.
Set scoping thresholds in writing: any account or data element that moves the sufficiency ratio by 1 percentage point or the Exhibit F record count by 0.5% is in scope.
Publish the scoping memo to the Chief Financial Officer and file it as the quarter's scoping evidence.
checklist.done: the PMIERs cycle in AuditBoard lists every in-scope account, sub-process and data element with a written, threshold-based scoping rationale.

checklist.step: Map each cited PMIERs section to the process and system that satisfies it
actions: Create one requirement row per cited section: Section 506 (internal audit), Section 304 (separation of responsibilities), Section 703 (Available and Minimum Required Assets).

Against Section 703, record the owning process (quarterly capital sufficiency computation), the owning role (Capital Management Manager) and the system of record (SAP S/4HANA plus the custodian holdings extract).
Against Section 304, record the three functions that must stay separate — underwriting, quality control, claims — and name the head of each from the HRIS org chart.
Against Section 506, record the internal audit charter reference, the reporting line to the Audit Committee, and the audit plan entry covering PMIERs.
Route the mapping to the Compliance Manager for confirmation that no cited section is left without an owning control.
checklist.done: every cited PMIERs section has a named process, owning role, system of record and at least one control id.

checklist.step: Write or refresh the control descriptions in the PMIERs control matrix
actions: For each control record the standard attributes: control id, PMIERs section, description, owner, frequency, preventive/detective, manual/automated, key/non-key, and the evidence artifact name.

Write descriptions in who-does-what-to-what form — e.g. 'Capital Management Manager recomputes Available Assets from the custodian holdings file and agrees the total to SAP S/4HANA account 1xxxx before the certification package is released'.
Delete or merge controls that no longer have an owner after the last reorganisation rather than carrying them as untested rows.
Have each named control owner accept ownership in AuditBoard so an unaccepted control shows as an open scoping issue.
Version the matrix with the quarter tag and lock the prior version read-only.
checklist.done: every matrix row has a testable description, an accepted owner, a frequency and a named evidence artifact, under a locked quarter version.

checklist.step: Stand up the controls over the quarterly Available Assets computation
actions: Take the quarter-end holdings and market values from the custodian file loaded into BlackRock Aladdin and reconcile CUSIP-level positions and fair values to Schedule D of the statutory ledger.

Apply the PMIERs Section 703 asset eligibility screen: exclude assets not held by the approved insurer, affiliate receivables and any asset not available to pay claims, and document the exclusion reason per line.
Compute Available Assets and agree the total to the general ledger cash and invested asset accounts in SAP S/4HANA; investigate and clear any variance over the documented tolerance before release.
Have the Chief Investment Officer confirm in writing that no in-scope holding is pledged, encumbered or subject to a repurchase obligation that would disqualify it.
Save the roll-forward workbook, custodian file and sign-offs as the control evidence for the quarter.
checklist.done: Available Assets tie to the custodian holdings and the general ledger, with every eligibility exclusion reasoned and an unencumbered confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Stand up the controls over Minimum Required Assets and the Exhibit A factors
actions: Load the quarter-end insured portfolio into the actuarial platform stratified by the Exhibit A dimensions: original LTV band, credit score band, vintage, performing / non-performing status and delinquency bucket.
Confirm the factor table loaded in the model matches the current PMIERs Exhibit A table published by the Enterprises, including any amendment factors, and record the table version and effective date.

Apply the required risk-based asset factor by loan, sum to gross MRA, then apply the permitted credits (approved risk transfer, reinsurance) only where the Head of Reinsurance confirms the transaction remains Enterprise-approved.
Recompute the PMIERs sufficiency ratio = Available Assets / Minimum Required Assets and record it to two decimal places with the dollar cushion.
Hand the MRA output and factor version note to the Controller for inclusion in the certification package.
checklist.done: MRA is computed from a version-stamped Exhibit A table, credits are supported by approved transactions, and the sufficiency ratio and cushion are recorded.

checklist.step: Control the completeness and accuracy of the Exhibit F loan-level dataset
actions: Run the Exhibit F build job in Snowflake and reconcile the record count and risk-in-force total to the policy administration inventory at the same quarter-end cut.

Execute the field-level validation suite over every Exhibit F column — loan identifier, Enterprise loan number, certificate number, original and current LTV, credit score, delinquency status, coverage percentage — and fail the run on any null or out-of-domain value in a required field.
Reconcile delinquency status counts to the servicer reporting feed and clear any difference with the Claims Director / Manager before the file is released.
Log the run id, row count, exception count and the analyst who released the file, and store the released file hash so the submitted version can be proven later.
Hand the release note to the Regulatory Reporting Manager who transmits the dataset to both Enterprises.
checklist.done: the Exhibit F file reconciles on record count and risk in force, has zero required-field validation failures, and the released version is hashed and logged.

checklist.step: Enforce Section 304 separation of responsibilities in the access model
actions: Build a segregation-of-duties ruleset in SailPoint IGA that makes underwriting approval, quality control review and claims authorisation mutually exclusive entitlements for mortgage guaranty applications.
Add a rule preventing anyone who prepares the Available Assets or MRA workpaper from holding the posting entitlement to the related SAP S/4HANA accounts.
Run the violation report for the quarter, and for each hit either remove the entitlement or record a documented compensating control approved by the Chief Risk Officer.
Certify the mortgage guaranty entitlement population in the quarterly access campaign and record non-responding managers as exceptions.
Export the clean violation report as evidence against the Section 304 control row.
checklist.done: the SoD ruleset is live, the quarter's violation report is clear or every hit carries an approved compensating control, and the access certification is complete.

checklist.step: Reconcile the PMIERs numbers to the statutory financial statements
actions: Tie Available Assets to statutory capital and surplus per the quarterly statement, bridging every reconciling item — non-admitted assets, contingency reserve, unearned premium reserve — on a signed bridge schedule.
Tie the insured portfolio risk in force in Exhibit F to the mortgage guaranty exhibit in the NAIC quarterly statement and explain any difference in scope.
Confirm the contingency reserve movement for the quarter follows the statutory 50% of earned premium contribution and the release rules, and document the calculation.
Have the Controller review and initial the bridge before the certification package is assembled.
checklist.done: a signed bridge reconciles Available Assets and risk in force to the filed NAIC quarterly statement with every reconciling item explained.

checklist.step: Operate the Section 506 internal audit function over the PMIERs processes
actions: Confirm the internal audit charter states the functional reporting line to the Audit Committee and the administrative line outside Finance, as Section 506 requires for independence.

Build the annual audit plan to cover, at least annually, underwriting, quality control, claims and PMIERs financial reporting, and get the plan approved by the Audit Committee with the approval minuted.
Staff each PMIERs engagement with auditors who have no operational role in the process being audited, and record the independence declaration per auditor per engagement.
Issue each report with a rating, findings, management responses and agreed remediation dates, addressed to the Audit Committee.
Track the plan's completion percentage quarterly and report any deferred PMIERs coverage to the Audit Committee with the reason.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee-approved plan covers underwriting, QC, claims and PMIERs reporting annually, with independence declarations and rated reports on file.

checklist.step: Assemble and review the quarterly PMIERs certification package
actions: Assemble the package: Available Assets roll-forward, MRA computation with the Exhibit A table version, sufficiency ratio and cushion, statutory bridge, Exhibit F release note and the open-deficiency listing.
Enter the submission due date as quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and confirm the transmission channel for each Enterprise before the final week.
Circulate the package to the Chief Financial Officer for review at quarter-end plus 35 days, capturing the review comments and their resolution.
Obtain the Controller's signature on the certification statement and transmit to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, saving both submission acknowledgements.
File the signed package, acknowledgements and workpapers in the financial reporting repository under the quarter.
checklist.done: the signed certification package and both Enterprise acknowledgements are filed, dated inside the 45-calendar-day window.

checklist.step: Set the evidence standard and retention for every PMIERs control
actions: For each matrix row define the acceptable evidence: system-generated report with run date and parameters, signed reconciliation, or dated approval — screenshots alone are not acceptable for key controls.
Apply a 7-year retention label from the certification date to the PMIERs folder so the record survives beyond the examination cycle.
Index the repository so a quarter's package can be retrieved by quarter-end date, PMIERs section and control id.
Run a completeness sweep at quarter-end plus 30 days and chase any control owner whose evidence slot is still empty.
checklist.done: every key control has a defined evidence type, the quarter's evidence slots are full, and the folder carries the 7-year retention label.

checklist.step: Rate and route control deficiencies as they arise
actions: Raise every failed control as an issue with the control id, the quarter, what failed and the dollar or record-count effect on Available Assets, MRA or Exhibit F.
Apply the rating rubric: any error that would change the reported sufficiency ratio or cause a late Enterprise submission is Significant; anything else is a Deficiency or Observation.
Assess aggregation across issues each quarter — several small Exhibit F field errors in the same data domain aggregate upward.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and require a re-test result before the issue can be closed.
Report the open issue population, ratings and ageing to the Controller and the Chief Audit Executive monthly.
checklist.done: every failed control has a rated, owned issue with a remediation date and a re-test gate before closure.

checklist.step: Escalate any Available Assets shortfall the moment it is identified
actions: Treat any quarter where Available Assets fall below Minimum Required Assets as a failure of the PMIERs financial requirements, not a measurement variance.
Notify both Enterprise relationship managers in writing within 30 calendar days of identification, stating the shortfall amount, the cause and the remediation plan.

Convene the Chief Risk Officer, Head of Capital Management and Chief Investment Officer to produce a remediation plan with dated actions — capital contribution, risk transfer, or new business restriction.
Brief the Board Governance Lead so the shortfall and plan reach the next board meeting and appear in the minutes.
Track the plan to closure and report the restored sufficiency ratio to the Enterprises.
checklist.done: any shortfall is reported to both Enterprises within 30 calendar days with a dated remediation plan minuted at board level.

checklist.step: Report PMIERs control status to the Audit Committee
actions: Place a standing PMIERs item on each quarterly Audit Committee agenda in the board portal.
Upload the pack: sufficiency ratio trend, control matrix testing results, open Significant deficiencies with ageing, and the Section 506 audit plan completion percentage.
Minute the committee's questions, the management commitments made and the dates given.
Carry forward unresolved commitments onto the next agenda rather than closing them at the meeting.
checklist.done: each quarter's minutes record the PMIERs control status, the sufficiency ratio and dated management commitments.

checklist.step: Refresh the control matrix whenever PMIERs changes
actions: Subscribe to the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac PMIERs pages and the FHFA news feed, and log each amendment, FAQ or Enterprise letter in the Internal Regulatory System with its effective date.
For the 2024 Available Asset standard amendment, record the 24-month phase-in milestones and the 9/30/2026 full-effectiveness date as dated change tasks.
Perform an impact assessment per change naming the affected control ids, systems and workpapers, and hand it to the Controller.
Update the control matrix and the procedure document within 30 calendar days of the change taking effect, and re-approve at the Chief Financial Officer level.
checklist.done: every PMIERs amendment is logged with an impact assessment and the matrix and procedure are updated within 30 calendar days of effectiveness.

testing.step: Build the population of PMIERs controls and submissions for the period
actions: Export the locked PMIERs control matrix for each quarter in the period, with control id, key/non-key flag, owner and frequency.
Add the four quarterly certification packages and the four Exhibit F datasets, taking submission dates and acknowledgements from the financial reporting repository.
Reconcile the control count to the prior period's matrix and obtain a written explanation for every control added, retired or de-scoped.
testing.done: the control and submission population is exported, reconciled to the prior period and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the control matrix back to the cited PMIERs sections
actions: Read Sections 304, 506 and 703 of PMIERs and list the discrete obligations each imposes.
Match each obligation to at least one key control in the matrix and mark any obligation with no control as a coverage gap.
Check the reverse direction: any control claiming a PMIERs section that the section does not actually require is flagged as mis-mapped.
testing.done: every obligation in the cited sections maps to a key control, and coverage gaps and mis-mappings are listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the control sample
actions: Take 100% of key controls over Available Assets, MRA and Exhibit F — these drive the sufficiency ratio.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 non-key controls from the remaining matrix, minimum 40 rows overall.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and the quarter tested so the sample can be re-drawn by a reviewer.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of ratio-driving key controls plus a reproducible random selection, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the Available Assets computation independently
actions: Take the custodian quarter-end holdings file directly from the custodian, not from Finance, and load it for independent computation.
Apply the Section 703 eligibility screen yourself and reach your own Available Assets total before opening the Finance workpaper.
Compare your total to the certified figure; any difference above the documented tolerance is an exception regardless of direction.
Trace ten of the largest positions to the custodian statement and to the Schedule D line in the statutory statement.
testing.done: an independent Available Assets total exists, is compared to the certified figure, and the ten largest positions are traced to custodian and Schedule D.

testing.step: Re-perform the MRA factor application on a loan sample
actions: Select 40 loans stratified across performing, delinquent and non-performing buckets from the quarter's Exhibit F dataset.
For each loan look up the required asset factor in the published PMIERs Exhibit A table for its LTV band, credit score band, vintage and delinquency status.
Recompute the required asset amount by hand in Excel and compare to the model output, listing every difference with the driving attribute.
Confirm the Exhibit A table version used by the model matches the version in force at the measurement date.
testing.done: 40 loans are independently factored, differences are listed by driving attribute and the factor table version is confirmed as in force.

testing.step: Trace Exhibit F fields to the servicing and policy systems
actions: Pick 30 loans from the submitted Exhibit F file and trace certificate number, coverage percentage, original LTV, credit score and delinquency status back to the policy administration record and the servicer file.
Confirm the submitted file hash matches the hash logged at release so the tested file is provably the submitted file.
Re-run the record count and risk-in-force reconciliation for the quarter and compare to the release note figures.
testing.done: 30 loans trace field-by-field to source, the file hash matches the release log, and the count and risk-in-force reconciliation reproduces.

testing.step: Test Section 304 separation of responsibilities in practice
actions: Export mortgage guaranty entitlements from SailPoint IGA and test whether any individual holds underwriting approval together with quality control or claims authorisation.
Take 15 claim decisions from the quarter and confirm the decider did not underwrite or QC the same certificate, using the system audit trail rather than the org chart.
Check that every compensating control recorded against an SoD hit has a dated Chief Risk Officer approval and evidence that it actually operated.
testing.done: no tested individual breaches the underwriting / QC / claims separation, or each breach carries an approved and operating compensating control.

testing.step: Recompute the submission timing and the shortfall notification clock
actions: For each quarter, compute quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and compare it to the Enterprise acknowledgement timestamps for the certification and the Exhibit F dataset.
Compare the annual audited package submission date to the April 15 deadline.
Where a shortfall was identified in the period, compute identification date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the date of the written notice to each Enterprise.
Treat any submission after the computed date as a fail with no materiality argument available.
testing.done: every submission and notification date is recomputed against its deadline and any lateness is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an AuditBoard issue per exception carrying the control id, quarter, the effect on the sufficiency ratio or Exhibit F, and the PMIERs section breached.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — stale Exhibit A table, source data defect, missing review, access conflict, calendar miss — plus an owner.
Set the remediation date and assess aggregation of related exceptions into a Significant deficiency.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed set, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate for key and non-key controls separately and compare each to the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the reviewing auditor, who prepared none of the sampled workpapers, sign the workpaper set.
Present the conclusion and open Significant deficiencies to the Audit Committee via the board portal and file the workpapers under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rates and the Audit Committee has received it on a minuted date.

checklist.step: Read the 2024 amendment and translate it into testable classification rules
actions: Open the FHFA/Enterprises 2024 PMIERs amendment on the Available Asset standard and extract every asset-class distinction it draws by credit quality and by liquidity.
Write each distinction as a rule with an objective test — rating threshold and rating agency used, marketability test, and the treatment where ratings split between agencies.
Extract the limits imposed on assets backed by residential mortgages and on assets backed by commercial real estate, stating the denominator each limit is measured against.
Record the 24-month phase-in schedule with the percentage applied at each quarter-end through full effectiveness on September 30, 2026.
Log the rule set in the Internal Regulatory System against REG-050 and route to the Chief Investment Officer and Chief Risk Officer for confirmation.
checklist.done: every amendment distinction and limit exists as an objectively testable rule with its phase-in percentage and a dated confirmation from CIO and CRO.

checklist.step: Load the rules into the investment system so classification happens at source
actions: In Aladdin create a PMIERs eligibility attribute on each security carrying the credit-quality bucket, the liquidity bucket and the collateral type (RMBS / CRE / other).
Populate the attribute from the ratings and sector fields, using the lower of two ratings where agencies split, and flag any security where the attribute cannot be derived automatically.
Build the compliance rule that computes RMBS-backed and CRE-backed exposure against the limit denominator and warns as the limit is approached.
Have the Portfolio Manager clear every manually classified security in writing, recording the reason the automatic derivation failed.
Schedule the attribute refresh to run before each quarter-end measurement cut.
checklist.done: every holding carries a derived PMIERs eligibility attribute, manual classifications are individually approved, and the limit rule runs before each measurement date.

checklist.step: Build the annual test programme over the amended standard
actions: Write the test programme in AuditBoard with one test step per rule: credit-quality bucketing, liquidity bucketing, RMBS limit, CRE limit, phase-in percentage application and the flow into Available Assets.
State the sample basis per step — 100% for limit computations, seeded random 60 securities for bucketing — and the pass threshold for each.
Book the fieldwork window so the draft report lands ahead of the April 15 annual reporting date.
Assign auditors with no investment operations role and record their independence declarations against the engagement.
checklist.done: an approved test programme exists with per-step sample bases, thresholds, an April 15-aligned timetable and independence declarations.

checklist.step: Cut the tested holdings population at each quarter-end measurement date
actions: Extract the full holdings list at each quarter-end with CUSIP, par, book value, fair value, ratings by agency, sector, collateral type and the derived PMIERs attribute.
Reconcile the extract to the custodian holdings statement on position count and market value and clear differences before use.
Reconcile market value to Schedule D of the statutory statement and document reconciling items such as trade-date versus settlement-date timing.
Sign the extract as complete and lock it so later portfolio activity cannot alter the tested population.
checklist.done: a locked, signed holdings extract per measurement date reconciles to both the custodian statement and Schedule D.

checklist.step: Re-perform the credit-quality and liquidity bucketing
actions: Take a seeded random sample of 60 securities stratified across corporate, structured, municipal and government sectors.
For each, pull the current ratings from Bloomberg (Moody's, S&P, Fitch) at the measurement date and apply the amendment's rating threshold and split-rating rule yourself.
Assess the liquidity bucket against the amendment's marketability test using issue size, trading activity and pricing source, and record the evidence for each call.
Compare your bucket to the Aladdin attribute and list every difference with the dollar par affected and the direction of the effect on Available Assets.
checklist.done: 60 securities are independently bucketed against measurement-date ratings, and every difference from the system attribute is listed with its dollar effect.

checklist.step: Compute and test the RMBS and CRE-backed asset limits
actions: Identify every holding backed by residential mortgages and every holding backed by commercial real estate, including agency and non-agency structures, and evidence the collateral determination from the offering document or Bloomberg security description.
Compute each exposure against the limit denominator specified by the amendment and express it as a percentage to two decimal places.
Compare the result to the limit in force at that measurement date after the phase-in percentage and record the headroom or the breach amount.
Where headroom is under 10% of the limit, notify the Chief Investment Officer in writing so trading can be constrained before quarter-end.
checklist.done: RMBS and CRE-backed exposures are computed against the in-force limits with the collateral determination evidenced and headroom or breach quantified.

checklist.step: Test the phase-in application at each quarter-end
actions: Rebuild the 24-month phase-in schedule from the amendment text, listing the percentage applicable at each quarter-end through September 30, 2026.
Compare the percentage actually applied in each quarter's Available Assets computation to your schedule and note any early or late application.
Recompute Available Assets for one quarter using your schedule and quantify the difference from the certified figure.
Confirm the tracker shows the remaining milestones with owners so the final step to full effectiveness is not missed.
checklist.done: the applied phase-in percentage agrees to an independently rebuilt schedule at every quarter-end, with any difference quantified.

checklist.step: Trace the tested classification through to the certified Available Assets figure
actions: Take the Available Assets roll-forward used in the quarterly PMIERs certification and agree its opening invested asset balance to SAP S/4HANA.
Confirm every exclusion and haircut in the roll-forward is driven by the tested classification attribute and not by a manual override.
List every manual journal or override affecting Available Assets, obtain the preparer's rationale and the approver's name, and test whether the approver was independent of the preparer.
Quantify the aggregate effect of misclassifications found in testing as a percentage of Minimum Required Assets.
checklist.done: the roll-forward traces to the ledger, every manual override is identified with an independent approver, and the aggregate misclassification effect is quantified.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and issue the draft report
actions: Rate each finding using the stated thresholds — over 0.5% of MRA overstatement or any limit breach is Significant.
Write each finding as condition, criteria (the amendment clause), cause, effect in dollars, and recommendation.
Issue the draft to the Head of Capital Management and Chief Investment Officer with a 10-business-day response window.
Reject management responses that lack a named owner or a dated action and return them for rework.
checklist.done: every finding is rated against the stated thresholds and carries a management response with a named owner and a dated action.

checklist.step: Agree remediation plans for each finding
actions: For classification findings, correct the Aladdin attribute and state the quarter in which the corrected figure will reach the PMIERs computation.
For limit breaches, agree the trading or hedging action with the Chief Investment Officer and record the date the exposure returns inside the limit.
For rule-derivation failures, raise a change request to the Aladdin ruleset with a target release date.
Set every remediation date within 30 calendar days of report issuance unless a longer date is approved in writing by the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: each finding has a remediation action, an owner and a date within 30 calendar days of issuance or a written CRO extension.

checklist.step: Restate and resubmit where a prior certification was overstated
actions: Where testing shows a prior quarter's Available Assets were overstated, recompute the sufficiency ratio for that quarter on the corrected basis.
Where the corrected ratio would have shown a shortfall, notify both Enterprises in writing within 30 calendar days of identification with the corrected figures.
Prepare the corrected certification exhibit, obtain the Controller's signature and transmit it, retaining both acknowledgements.
File the restatement memo, corrected exhibit and acknowledgements alongside the original quarter's package.
checklist.done: any overstated quarter is recomputed, corrected with the Enterprises where required within 30 calendar days, and the restatement is filed with the original package.

checklist.step: Retest remediated controls and close the findings
actions: Retest within 45 calendar days of each stated remediation date using a fresh sample, never the same securities used in the original test.
For limit findings, re-run the exposure computation at the next measurement date and confirm the exposure is inside the in-force limit.
Record the retest evidence against the finding and close only on a passing retest — management assertion alone does not close a finding.
Escalate any finding that fails retest twice to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: each finding is closed only on a passing retest performed within 45 calendar days on a fresh sample, or escalated after a second failure.

checklist.step: Report the annual test result into the April 15 package
actions: Finalise the report with the overall opinion on the amended Available Asset standard controls and the classification accuracy rate achieved.
Include the phase-in status showing which percentage applies now and what remains before September 30, 2026.
Present to the Audit Committee via the board portal and have the discussion and any committee direction minuted.
Hand the final report to the Controller for inclusion in the annual PMIERs package submitted by April 15.
checklist.done: the signed annual report with the classification accuracy rate and phase-in status is minuted at the Audit Committee and included in the April 15 package.

checklist.step: Feed the results back into the classification rules and portfolio limits
actions: Amend the investment policy statement's eligible-asset schedule where testing showed the policy permitted assets the amendment penalises.
Set internal warning limits inside the PMIERs RMBS and CRE limits so quarter-end breaches are prevented rather than detected.
Brief the Portfolio Manager and Trader on the classification errors found so the same securities are not repurchased into the wrong bucket.
Confirm the amended limits are coded in Aladdin compliance and produce a pre-trade warning.
checklist.done: the investment policy and Aladdin pre-trade limits reflect the amendment, with internal warning limits set inside the PMIERs limits.

checklist.step: Track phase-in milestones through to September 30, 2026
actions: Maintain a milestone row per quarter-end through September 30, 2026 with the applicable percentage, the owner and the readiness status.
At each quarter-end confirm the applied percentage matches the milestone row before the certification package is released.
Model the fully phased-in position each quarter and report the projected sufficiency ratio at full effectiveness to the Chief Financial Officer.
Escalate to the Chief Risk Officer where the projected fully phased-in ratio falls below the internal cushion target.
checklist.done: every phase-in milestone through September 30, 2026 has an owner and a status, and the fully phased-in projected ratio is reported quarterly.

testing.step: Build the population of assets claimed as Available Assets
actions: Extract, for each quarter-end in the year, every security claimed in Available Assets with CUSIP, par, fair value, agency ratings, collateral type and the derived PMIERs bucket.
Add securities excluded from Available Assets so exclusion decisions are testable, not just inclusions.
Reconcile the total to the certified Available Assets figure and to the invested asset balance in SAP S/4HANA, explaining every reconciling item.
testing.done: the population covers included and excluded securities and reconciles to both the certified figure and the ledger.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the custodian record of ownership
actions: Obtain the custodian holdings statement at each measurement date directly from the custodian.
Match position by position on CUSIP and par and list any security in the Available Assets population that the custodian does not confirm the insurer holds.
Confirm no matched position is flagged as pledged, on loan or subject to a repurchase agreement, since such assets are not available to pay claims.
testing.done: every claimed asset is confirmed by the custodian as held and unencumbered, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the classification sample
actions: Take 100% of securities with a manually assigned PMIERs bucket and 100% of RMBS and CRE-backed holdings.
Take a seeded random sample of 60 remaining securities stratified by sector and by dollar size band.
Record the seed, the population size, the strata and the draw date so the reviewer can re-draw the identical sample.
testing.done: the sample covers all manual classifications and all RMBS/CRE holdings plus a reproducible stratified random selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the bucket assignment against measurement-date ratings
actions: For each sampled security pull the Moody's, S&P and Fitch ratings as at the measurement date, not today's ratings.
Apply the amendment's credit-quality threshold and split-rating convention to reach your own bucket before opening the recorded bucket.
Apply the liquidity test using issue size, pricing source and observed trading, recording the evidence relied on.
List every difference with the par amount and whether it overstates or understates Available Assets.
testing.done: each sampled security has an independent bucket derived from measurement-date ratings, with all differences quantified by direction.

testing.step: Recompute the RMBS and CRE-backed limits
actions: Rebuild the RMBS-backed and CRE-backed exposure from the population using your own collateral determinations, evidenced from offering documents.
Compute each against the amendment's denominator and compare to the limit in force at that measurement date after phase-in.
Recompute the effect on Available Assets of any excess over the limit and compare it to the treatment applied by management.
Treat any breach at any measurement date as an automatic fail regardless of subsequent remediation.
testing.done: both limits are independently recomputed at every measurement date and any breach is recorded as an automatic fail.

testing.step: Recompute the phase-in percentage applied each quarter
actions: Rebuild the 24-month phase-in schedule from the amendment and derive the percentage applicable at each quarter-end through September 30, 2026.
Compare to the percentage embedded in each quarter's computation and quantify the Available Assets difference from any mismatch.
Confirm no quarter applied a future, more favourable phase-in step early.
testing.done: the applied phase-in percentage is confirmed against an independently rebuilt schedule for every quarter, with differences quantified.

testing.step: Test the effect on the certified sufficiency ratio
actions: Aggregate every classification, limit and phase-in exception into a corrected Available Assets figure per quarter.
Recompute the sufficiency ratio as corrected Available Assets divided by the reported Minimum Required Assets.
Compare the corrected ratio to the certified ratio and to 1.00, identifying any quarter that would have shown a shortfall.
Express the aggregate overstatement as a percentage of MRA and compare it to the 0.5% fail threshold.
testing.done: a corrected sufficiency ratio exists for every quarter, is compared to the certified ratio and to the 0.5% of MRA threshold.

testing.step: Verify that identified overstatements were reported to the Enterprises
actions: For any quarter whose corrected ratio falls below 1.00, locate the written notification to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and read its content.
Compute identification date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the notification date on each Enterprise acknowledgement.
Confirm the notification stated the shortfall amount, the cause and the remediation plan rather than a general statement.
testing.done: every corrected shortfall has a dated Enterprise notification inside 30 calendar days that states amount, cause and plan.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the CUSIP or limit affected, the dollar effect and the amendment clause breached.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — stale rating feed, split-rating rule error, collateral misidentification, phase-in schedule error, manual override — and an owner.
Set the remediation date within 30 calendar days of report issuance and record the retest date 45 calendar days later.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's rolling test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue with a fixed-set root cause, an owner, a 30-day remediation date and a booked retest.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the classification accuracy rate on the sample and compare it to the 98% threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — supported by the workpaper references and the corrected ratio analysis.
Have an Internal Auditor who performed none of the sampled classification work sign the workpaper set.
Present the report to the Audit Committee via the board portal and hand the signed report to the Controller for the April 15 package.
testing.done: a signed report states the accuracy rate and conclusion and is minuted at the Audit Committee before the April 15 filing.

checklist.step: Open the engagement acceptance file for the audit year
actions: Create the engagement acceptance folder in the board portal Audit Committee workspace named <firm>-<audit year> and set the acceptance decision date at least 45 calendar days before planned fieldwork.

Ask the Controller for the scope of statements the firm will audit — mortgage guaranty statutory statements, GAAP consolidated statements and any Available Assets schedule relied on for the PMIERs annual package.
List the proposed engagement partner, concurring review partner, and the engagement quality reviewer, with the year each first served the entity.
Circulate the acceptance timetable to the Audit Committee chair and to the Chief Financial Officer.
checklist.done: an acceptance folder exists with the audited scope, the proposed partner roster with first-year-of-service dates and a decision date 45 days ahead of fieldwork.

checklist.step: Request and read the firm's written independence communication
actions: Request the PCAOB Rule 3526 letter from the engagement partner, addressed to the Audit Committee, before any fieldwork begins.
Confirm the letter describes all relationships between the firm, its network and the company that may bear on independence, and states the firm's independence conclusion.
Compare the relationships disclosed against the company's own record of services purchased from the firm and its network, and query any omission in writing.
Upload the letter and the query correspondence to the engagement acceptance folder for the committee pack.
checklist.done: a Rule 3526 letter addressed to the committee is on file, reconciled to the company's own service record, with every discrepancy queried in writing.

checklist.step: Build the partner and senior staff tenure schedule
actions: Request from the firm a schedule of every partner and senior manager assigned to the engagement showing the first and most recent year of service on this entity.
Compute consecutive years of service per partner and flag anyone entering their fifth consecutive year as due to rotate off.
Confirm any partner who previously rotated off has served the required five-year time-out before returning.
Record the planned rotation year for each current partner so the committee sees the succession, not just the current position.
checklist.done: a tenure schedule shows consecutive years and planned rotation year per partner, with anyone at five consecutive years flagged.

checklist.step: Determine the rotation position and require successors where needed
actions: Where a lead or concurring partner reaches five consecutive years, require the firm to name a successor before acceptance and record the successor's independence confirmation.
Meet the incoming partner and record the committee's assessment of their mortgage guaranty and PMIERs experience in the minutes.
Require a documented transition plan covering the Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets audit areas so continuity is not used as a reason to defer rotation.
Record the committee's rotation determination as a resolution with the effective audit year.
checklist.done: no partner serves a sixth consecutive year, each successor is named, assessed and minuted, and a transition plan covers the PMIERs balances.

checklist.step: Run every non-audit service through pre-approval
actions: Block purchase orders naming the audit firm or a network firm in the procurement system so they route to the Audit Committee pre-approval queue instead of a normal buyer.
For each request record the service description, the requesting function, the fee and the reason the audit firm rather than another provider is proposed.

Test each against the prohibited-service list — bookkeeping, financial information system design and implementation, valuation or actuarial services feeding the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resource functions, broker-dealer or investment services, legal services — and reject rather than escalate anything on the list.
Route surviving requests to the Audit Committee for specific pre-approval, or confirm they fall inside a general pre-approval policy with the fee limit stated.
checklist.done: no purchase order to the audit firm can be raised without a recorded pre-approval, and prohibited services are rejected at intake.

checklist.step: Track audit and non-audit fees against the pre-approvals
actions: Extract all amounts invoiced by the audit firm and its network in the year from the accounts payable ledger by vendor and by cost centre.
Split the total into audit, audit-related, tax and all other fees using the invoice narrative, and agree the split to the pre-approval register line by line.
Investigate any invoice with no matching pre-approval and any invoice exceeding its pre-approved fee limit before it is paid.
Hand the reconciled fee analysis to the Corporate Secretary for the committee pack and for the proxy or annual report disclosure.
checklist.done: the ledger fee split agrees line by line to the pre-approval register, with unapproved or over-limit invoices stopped before payment.

checklist.step: Test the employment cooling-off position for finance hires
actions: Run a Workday report of hires and internal moves in the year into roles with financial reporting oversight — Chief Financial Officer, Controller, Chief Accounting Officer, and any role signing the PMIERs certification.
For each, check whether the individual was employed by the audit firm and whether they participated in the company's audit in any capacity.
Where they did, confirm a full annual audit period elapsed between their last participation and the start of employment, and evidence the dates from the firm.
Escalate any position where the cooling-off period cannot be evidenced to General Counsel before the offer is confirmed.
checklist.done: every financial reporting oversight hire is screened, and any ex-audit-firm hire has an evidenced one-year cooling-off or a General Counsel decision on file.

checklist.step: Screen personal financial and family relationships
actions: Issue the annual independence questionnaire to officers, directors and finance staff in the GRC platform asking about holdings in the audit firm, employment of close family members at the firm, and business relationships with it.
Chase non-responses weekly and record a nil-response as an open exception, not as a clean answer.
Assess each positive response for whether it creates a covered-person relationship and refer those that do to General Counsel.
Summarise the responses and the assessments for the engagement acceptance pack.
checklist.done: every questionnaire is returned and assessed, with positive responses referred and summarised in the acceptance pack.

checklist.step: Confirm the firm's qualification to audit a PMIERs approved insurer
actions: Confirm the firm is registered with the PCAOB and is in good standing, and record the most recent PCAOB inspection report date.
Confirm the firm meets the domiciliary state's qualified independent certified public accountant definition and that any required awareness letter has been filed with the insurance department.
Confirm the engagement team includes staff experienced in mortgage guaranty insurance and in the PMIERs Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets computation.
Record the conclusion in the acceptance memo with the supporting registrations attached.
checklist.done: the firm's PCAOB registration, state qualification and mortgage guaranty experience are evidenced in the acceptance memo.

checklist.step: Take the acceptance decision at the Audit Committee
actions: Table the acceptance pack — Rule 3526 letter, tenure schedule, fee analysis, questionnaire summary, qualification memo — at the committee meeting.
Record the committee's independence determination as an explicit resolution naming the firm, the engagement partner and the audit year.
Record the pre-approval policy for the year including any general pre-approval categories and their fee limits.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute the discussion, the determination and any conditions attached.
checklist.done: the minutes carry an explicit independence determination naming firm, partner and year, plus the year's pre-approval policy.

checklist.step: Report pre-approvals and fees to the committee each quarter
actions: Place a standing item on each quarterly Audit Committee agenda covering services pre-approved, services delivered and fees incurred year to date against limits.
Highlight any general pre-approval category approaching its fee limit so the committee can act before it is breached.
Report any service delivered without pre-approval as an exception item, not inside the routine schedule.
Minute the committee's ratification or rejection of each exception.
checklist.done: each quarter's minutes record delivered services, fees against limits and the disposition of any unapproved service.

checklist.step: Assess and document any potential impairment
actions: On any breach — unapproved service, prohibited service, tenure overrun, cooling-off failure — open an impairment assessment file in iManage within five business days.
Analyse whether the relationship created a mutual or conflicting interest, an audit of the firm's own work, a management function or an advocacy role.
Obtain the firm's written analysis of whether its independence was impaired for the period and compare it against your own.
Recommend the remedy — service termination, fee disgorgement, partner replacement, or re-audit — and route to the Audit Committee for decision.
checklist.done: every breach has a dated impairment assessment holding both the company's and the firm's analysis and a recommended remedy.

checklist.step: Obtain the year-end independence reconfirmation
actions: Request an updated Rule 3526 communication from the firm at the conclusion of the audit and before the report is released.
Confirm it covers the full period audited, including any services accepted after the original acceptance decision.
Compare it to the year's pre-approval register and question any service the firm does not disclose.
File the reconfirmation in the engagement folder as the closing independence evidence.
checklist.done: a year-end independence reconfirmation covering the full audit period is on file and reconciled to the pre-approval register.

checklist.step: Retain the independence record and index it for examination
actions: Move the engagement folder into the compliance evidence repository indexed by audit year, firm and engagement partner.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the audit report date.
Confirm the index allows retrieval of the tenure schedule and pre-approval register on their own, since examiners request them separately.
Run an annual completeness check that every audit year since the retention window opened has a complete folder.
checklist.done: each audit year's independence folder is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by year, firm and partner.

checklist.step: Refresh the procedure when independence rules change
actions: Monitor SEC, PCAOB and NAIC releases for changes to independence, rotation, cooling-off and pre-approval rules, and log each in the Internal Regulatory System.
Assess the effect on the prohibited-service list, the rotation clock and the general pre-approval categories.
Update the procedure and the Audit Committee charter, and table both for re-approval at the next committee meeting.
Brief Procurement so the purchase-order block list reflects the new prohibited services.
checklist.done: each rule change is logged, assessed, reflected in the procedure and charter, and pushed into the procurement block list.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements, partners, services and hires
actions: Extract every payment and accrual to the audit firm and any network firm in the year from accounts payable by vendor id, with invoice narrative and cost centre.
Add the engagement partner roster from the firm's tenure schedule and the list of financial reporting oversight hires from Workday.
Reconcile the ledger total to the fee disclosure prepared for the annual report and explain every difference.
testing.done: the population covers every fee, partner and relevant hire and reconciles to the disclosed fee split.

testing.step: Reconcile the fee population to the pre-approval register
actions: Match each invoice to a pre-approval entry on service description, provider entity and fee limit.
List every invoice with no matching pre-approval and every invoice whose cumulative fees exceed the approved limit.
Check the pre-approval date pre-dates the service start date, since after-the-fact approval is not pre-approval.
testing.done: every invoice matches a pre-approval dated before service start, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of non-audit service engagements and 100% of partners and senior managers on the tenure schedule.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 audit-fee invoices and all financial reporting oversight hires in the year.
Record the seed, population sizes and draw date so the reviewer can reproduce the selection.
testing.done: all non-audit services and partners are covered plus a reproducible sample of audit invoices and hires.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited-service assessment
actions: Read the statement of work for each sampled non-audit service rather than relying on the invoice narrative.
Test each against the prohibited-service categories in SEC Regulation S-X Rule 2-01(c)(4) and the NAIC equivalent, reaching your own conclusion first.
Pay particular attention to actuarial and valuation work touching loss reserves or the Available Assets balance, since those feed the PMIERs computation.
List every service you would have rejected that was in fact approved.
testing.done: each sampled service has an independent prohibited-service conclusion drawn from the statement of work, with disagreements listed.

testing.step: Recompute partner tenure and rotation timing
actions: Rebuild each partner's consecutive years of service from the firm's engagement letters and audit reports rather than from the summary schedule.
Identify any lead or concurring partner in a sixth consecutive year and any returning partner whose time-out was shorter than five years.
Compare your rebuilt schedule to the schedule the committee relied on and list every difference.
Confirm each rotation was minuted in the audit year it took effect.
testing.done: tenure is rebuilt from primary documents, overruns and short time-outs are identified, and rotations tie to minutes.

testing.step: Trace the independence letters and the committee determination
actions: Locate the Rule 3526 letter for the year and confirm it is addressed to the Audit Committee and dated before fieldwork began.
Locate the year-end reconfirmation and confirm it covers the full audit period.
Open the minutes and confirm an explicit independence determination naming firm, partner and audit year exists, not a general approval of the audit plan.
Confirm the relationships disclosed in the letters reconcile to the company's own fee and hire records.
testing.done: both independence letters exist with correct dating and scope and an explicit minuted determination reconciles to company records.

testing.step: Test the employment cooling-off screening
actions: Re-run the Workday report of financial reporting oversight hires independently of HR's extract and compare the two populations.
For each hire with audit firm history, obtain the firm's confirmation of last participation date and compute the gap to the employment start date.
Confirm any gap shorter than a full annual audit period was escalated to General Counsel with a documented decision.
testing.done: the hire population reproduces independently and every ex-firm hire has an evidenced gap or a documented General Counsel decision.

testing.step: Recompute the acceptance and reporting timing
actions: Compute planned fieldwork start minus 45 calendar days and compare it to the acceptance decision date in the minutes.
Compare the audit report date to the April 15 delivery date for the annual PMIERs package and confirm the sequence works without compressing acceptance.
Compare each quarterly pre-approval report date to the corresponding committee meeting date and flag any quarter with no report.
testing.done: acceptance, report and quarterly reporting dates are recomputed against their deadlines with every miss recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the service, partner or hire, the rule breached and whether an impairment assessment was opened.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — procurement block bypassed, service mischaracterised at intake, tenure tracked from the wrong start year, hire screening missed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any potential impairment, require General Counsel sign-off before closure.
Carry open exceptions into the next engagement acceptance as mandatory agenda items.
testing.done: each exception has an owned, root-caused issue with a remediation date and, where relevant, a General Counsel sign-off gate.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance threshold: one unapproved service, prohibited service, tenure overrun or cooling-off breach fails the control.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references and any impairment assessments attached.
Have an Internal Auditor who administers no part of the pre-approval workflow sign the workpaper set.
Report to the Audit Committee in closed session via the board portal and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the zero-tolerance threshold and has been reported in a minuted closed session.

checklist.step: Publish the annual audit and filing calendar
actions: Build the calendar backwards from the April 15 Enterprise delivery date, the June 1 state audited report date and the August 1 internal control communication date.
Load each milestone into BlackLine as a close task with an owner, a due date and a dependency on the preceding task.
Set the hard internal gates: trial balance final January 31, draft statements to the auditor February 28, audit report expected March 25, package assembled April 8.
Circulate the calendar to the Statutory Reporting Manager, the Head of Capital Management, the Chief Audit Executive and the engagement partner and obtain written agreement to the dates.
checklist.done: every milestone is a dated, owned BlackLine task and the auditor has agreed the report date in writing.

checklist.step: Close the mortgage guaranty ledger and lock the balances
actions: Complete the December close for the approved insurer legal entity and confirm every balance sheet account has a signed reconciliation in BlackLine.
Confirm the contingency reserve, unearned premium reserve and loss and loss adjustment expense reserves are booked at the Appointed Actuary's certified amounts.
Lock the period in SAP S/4HANA so post-close entries require a documented request approved by the Controller.
Produce the locked trial balance and hand it to the Statutory Reporting Manager as the single source for the statements.
checklist.done: the period is locked, every account is reconciled and signed, and reserves agree to the actuarial certification.

checklist.step: Prepare the statutory annual statement and its mortgage guaranty exhibits
actions: Load the locked trial balance into the NAIC annual statement software and complete the Assets, Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds pages plus Schedule D for the invested asset detail.
Complete the mortgage guaranty exhibits including risk in force, insurance in force and the contingency reserve roll-forward.
Clear every NAIC cross-check and validation edit and retain the clean validation report as evidence.
Agree the statutory surplus figure to the Available Assets bridge prepared by the Head of Capital Management.
checklist.done: the annual statement passes all NAIC validations and its surplus ties to the Available Assets bridge.

checklist.step: Prepare the audited PMIERs schedules for the package
actions: Prepare the year-end Available Assets schedule showing eligible assets after the amended Available Asset standard, with the phase-in percentage applied at December 31 stated on the face.
Prepare the Minimum Required Assets schedule stratified on the Exhibit A dimensions with the factor table version recorded.
Compute the year-end sufficiency ratio and the dollar cushion and present the four quarter-ends as a trend.
Hand the schedules to the engagement team with the supporting custodian and loan-level files and record the handover date.
checklist.done: the Available Assets, MRA and sufficiency schedules are prepared, version-stamped and handed to the auditor with their support files.

checklist.step: Support the audit fieldwork and control the request log
actions: Open a SharePoint request tracker listing every auditor request with the requester, the owner, the due date and the delivery date.
Deliver items to the tracker only, so what was given to the auditor and when is provable at examination.
Escalate any request open beyond five business days to the responsible function head with a copy to the Chief Financial Officer.
Review the open request list against the March 25 report date weekly and re-plan if the slippage threatens April 15.
checklist.done: every auditor request is logged and dated in the tracker and the open list is compatible with the March 25 report date.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the draft representation letter and confirm every assertion has a workpaper behind it, particularly those on Available Assets eligibility, encumbrances and reserve adequacy.
Confirm the subsequent-events representation covers any post-year-end capital action or PMIERs-relevant Enterprise communication.
Have the Chief Executive Officer and Controller countersign as required by the firm.
Execute in DocuSign and file the executed letter in the financial reporting repository with the audit evidence.
checklist.done: an executed representation letter is on file with each assertion traceable to a workpaper.

checklist.step: Receive and read the auditor communications
actions: Collect the audit report, the AS 1301 communication with those charged with governance, the management letter and any communication of internal control related matters.
Confirm the audit opinion type — unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer — and flag any modification to the Chief Financial Officer and General Counsel the same day.
List every internal control deficiency the auditor raises, mapped to the PMIERs control matrix control id it affects.
Upload all communications to the board portal for the Audit Committee pack.
checklist.done: all auditor communications are received, the opinion type is recorded and every deficiency is mapped to a PMIERs control id.

checklist.step: Table the audited statements and communications at the Audit Committee
actions: Agenda the audited statements, the auditor communications and management's responses at the committee meeting before the April 15 delivery.
Arrange a closed session between the committee and the engagement partner with no management present and minute that it occurred.
Record the committee's recommendation that the board approve the statements and the date of the board resolution.
Minute management's response and remediation dates for each auditor-raised deficiency.
checklist.done: the minutes record the committee review, the closed session, the board approval resolution and dated responses to each deficiency.

checklist.step: Assemble the Enterprise package
actions: Assemble the package: audited statutory financial statements with the audit report, audited GAAP statements where required, the year-end Available Assets and MRA schedules, the sufficiency ratio trend and the auditor's internal control communication.
Run the contents checklist against the Enterprises' annual reporting requirements and record a reason for any item deliberately excluded.
Have the Controller review and sign the package cover certification.
Freeze the package as a versioned PDF set so what was sent can be proven later.
checklist.done: a signed, version-frozen package matches the Enterprise contents checklist with every exclusion reasoned.

checklist.step: Transmit to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac by April 15
actions: Transmit the package to each Enterprise through the mortgage insurer reporting channel each has designated, using the current named contacts confirmed within the last quarter.
Capture the submission confirmation or acknowledgement email from each Enterprise with its timestamp.
Where a channel rejects a file for size or format, resolve and resubmit the same day rather than waiting, and log both attempts.
File both acknowledgements against the package version in the repository.
checklist.done: both Enterprises have acknowledged receipt on or before April 15 and the acknowledgements are filed against the sent version.

checklist.step: File the audited statutory report with the domiciliary regulator
actions: File the audited statutory financial report with the domiciliary commissioner by June 1 and with any other state that requires a copy.
File the auditor's communication of internal control related matters by August 1 with management's response attached.
Where an extension is needed, request it in writing before the due date with the reason and the proposed date, and file the granted extension with the package.
Retain the state filing confirmations alongside the Enterprise acknowledgements.
checklist.done: the state audited report is filed by June 1 and the internal control communication by August 1, with confirmations retained.

checklist.step: Reconcile the Enterprise package to the state and public filings
actions: Tie surplus, total assets, risk in force and the contingency reserve in the Enterprise package to the same captions in the filed NAIC annual statement.
Tie the same figures to the holding company's public reporting where the insurer is consolidated, and explain consolidation differences in a bridge.
Document any presentational difference between packages so a reader comparing them finds the explanation already written.
Have the Controller initial the bridge before it is filed.
checklist.done: an initialled bridge reconciles the Enterprise package to the NAIC statement and to public reporting, with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Notify the Enterprises immediately of a modified opinion or auditor change
actions: Where the opinion is qualified, adverse or disclaimed, notify both Enterprise relationship managers in writing within 30 calendar days of the report date, stating the basis and the remediation plan.
Where the auditor resigns or is dismissed, notify the domiciliary commissioner within five business days and the Enterprises in the same week.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording of every such notice before it is sent.
Brief the Audit Committee chair before, not after, the notice goes out.
checklist.done: any modified opinion or auditor change is notified inside its deadline on counsel-cleared wording with the committee chair pre-briefed.

checklist.step: Drive the auditor-raised deficiencies into the control matrix
actions: Open an AuditBoard issue for each deficiency in the auditor's communication, linked to the PMIERs control matrix control id it affects.
Record management's agreed action, owner and date, refusing any response without both.
Schedule the retest and require passing evidence before closure, then report status at each quarterly Audit Committee meeting.
Carry any deficiency open at the next year-end into the following audit's planning discussion.
checklist.done: every auditor deficiency is an owned, dated, retest-gated issue linked to a control id and reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Archive the annual filing record
actions: Move the frozen package version, both Enterprise acknowledgements, the state filing confirmations, all auditor communications and the representation letter into the repository under the audit year.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the audit report date.
Index by audit year, recipient (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, domiciliary state) and document type so examiners can be served a single recipient's file.
Confirm retrieval by running a test request for the prior year's Fannie Mae file.
checklist.done: the year's filing record is archived, retention-labelled and provably retrievable by recipient and document type.

testing.step: Build the population of annual filings and auditor communications
actions: List every package delivered in the year to Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the domiciliary state, with the version identifier and delivery date.
List every auditor communication received — audit report, AS 1301 communication, management letter, internal control communication — with its date.
Reconcile the list to the filing calendar in BlackLine and obtain a written explanation for any calendar milestone with no corresponding artifact.
testing.done: the filing and communication population is complete against the calendar with every gap explained in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile the delivered package back to the audited statements
actions: Open the frozen package version actually transmitted and compare it page for page to the signed audited statements.
Confirm the audit report in the package carries the firm's signature, the city and the report date.
Compare the Available Assets and MRA schedules in the package to the schedules the auditor examined and list any post-audit change.
testing.done: the transmitted package matches the signed statements and audited schedules with any post-audit change identified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of package contents
actions: Take 100% of the Available Assets, MRA and sufficiency ratio figures in the package as key items.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 other figures across the balance sheet, income statement and mortgage guaranty exhibits.
Record the seed, the population and the draw date so the selection can be reproduced.
testing.done: all PMIERs-critical figures plus a reproducible random sample of other figures are selected for tracing.

testing.step: Trace sampled figures to the audited ledger
actions: Trace each sampled figure to the locked December trial balance in SAP S/4HANA and to the signed account reconciliation behind it.
Confirm no post-lock journal changed a traced balance without a Controller-approved request.
For the Available Assets figure, agree the eligible asset total to the custodian statement and the phase-in percentage to the amendment schedule.
testing.done: every sampled figure traces to the locked ledger and its reconciliation, with post-lock entries individually approved.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadlines and compare to the acknowledgements
actions: Compare each Enterprise acknowledgement timestamp to April 15 and record any delivery after that date as a fail.
Compare the state audited report filing confirmation to June 1 and the internal control communication confirmation to August 1.
Where an extension was used, confirm the request pre-dates the original due date and that a written grant exists.
Where a modified opinion or auditor change occurred, compute report date plus 30 calendar days and dismissal date plus five business days and compare to the notices sent.
testing.done: every delivery and notification date is recomputed against its deadline with extensions evidenced and misses recorded as fails.

testing.step: Verify the auditor communications reached those charged with governance
actions: Match each auditor communication to an Audit Committee agenda and minute entry.
Confirm the closed session with the engagement partner without management is minuted for the year.
Confirm the board resolution approving the audited statements pre-dates the April 15 transmission.
Flag any communication received but never tabled as an automatic fail.
testing.done: every auditor communication is minuted, the closed session occurred, and board approval pre-dates transmission.

testing.step: Reconcile the Enterprise package to the state and public filings
actions: Compare surplus, total assets, risk in force and the contingency reserve between the Enterprise package and the filed NAIC annual statement.
Compare the same captions to the holding company's public reporting and test the consolidation bridge arithmetic.
Treat any unexplained difference as a fail, and any explained difference without a written bridge as a documentation exception.
testing.done: the three filings reconcile figure for figure or every difference is supported by a tested written bridge.

testing.step: Test the disposition of auditor-raised deficiencies
actions: Match each deficiency in the auditor's communication to an AuditBoard issue with a control id, owner and remediation date.
For deficiencies marked closed, inspect the retest evidence rather than the closure note.
Confirm each open deficiency was reported at every quarterly Audit Committee meeting since it was raised.
testing.done: every auditor deficiency has a linked issue, closures rest on retest evidence, and open items were reported quarterly.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the recipient affected, the deadline missed or the content defect, and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — close slippage, auditor report late, channel rejection, contents checklist gap, approval sequencing error — and an owner.
Set the remediation date and, for any late Enterprise delivery, require a Chief Financial Officer sign-off on the explanation given to the Enterprise.
Carry every open exception into next year's filing calendar as a pre-agreed checkpoint.
testing.done: each exception has a root-caused, owned issue with a remediation date and, for late deliveries, a CFO-signed explanation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance date threshold and the requirement that every auditor communication be tabled.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references and the recomputed dates behind it.
Have an Internal Auditor outside the Controller's organisation, who prepared none of the filed schedules, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late filings to the Audit Committee via the board portal and archive the workpaper with the year's filing record.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the date thresholds and has been reported to the committee and archived.
