checklist.step: Map the PMIERs financial requirement onto a named board committee
actions: Read Section 703 and record the discrete oversight obligations: continuous maintenance of Available Assets at or above Minimum Required Assets, quarterly measurement, and treatment of a shortfall as a failure of the financial requirements.

Assign each obligation to a named committee — capital sufficiency oversight to the risk committee, financial reporting integrity to the Audit Committee, asset eligibility policy to the investment committee.
Assign Section 701 capital sources and diversification oversight to the risk committee and record where the board itself retains the decision.
Publish the responsibility map in the board portal and have the Board Governance Lead confirm no obligation is unassigned.
checklist.done: every Section 701 and 703 oversight obligation is assigned to a named committee or to the board, with no unassigned obligation.

checklist.step: Write the obligations into the committee charters
actions: Amend the risk committee charter to require a quarterly review of the PMIERs sufficiency ratio, the dollar cushion and the forward projection to the fully phased-in Available Asset standard.
Amend the Audit Committee charter to state the Section 506 internal audit functional reporting line and the committee's approval of the internal audit plan and budget.
State quorum, meeting frequency, delegated authority limits and the escalation trigger to the full board on any projected shortfall.
Table the amended charters for board approval and record the approval resolution and effective date.
checklist.done: each charter names its PMIERs obligations, quorum, frequency and escalation trigger, approved by a dated board resolution.

checklist.step: Set and evidence committee composition and independence
actions: Build a composition schedule listing each director, their committee memberships, appointment date, term end and independence status.

Determine independence against the stated criteria — no employment with the company or its auditor, no material business relationship, no compensation other than director fees — and record the determination per director per year.
Confirm the Audit Committee includes at least one member with financial expertise covering insurance statutory reporting, and record the basis for that determination.
Identify seats falling vacant within 12 months and hand the succession requirement to the nominating process.
checklist.done: a current composition schedule records independence determinations, the financial expert designation and the 12-month vacancy pipeline.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly capital sufficiency pack
actions: Present Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets at the quarter-end measurement date, the sufficiency ratio to two decimals and the dollar cushion.
Show the four-quarter trend and the drivers of movement — new insurance written, cures and defaults, investment returns, capital actions and risk transfer.
Project the ratio forward four quarters under a base case and a housing-stress case, applying the phase-in percentages through September 30, 2026.
State the internal cushion target and the actions triggered if the projection breaches it, and identify the owner of each action.
checklist.done: the pack shows the measured ratio, its drivers, a four-quarter stressed projection on the phased-in basis and the triggered actions with owners.

checklist.step: Table the sufficiency pack at the risk committee each quarter
actions: Load the pack to the board portal at quarter-end plus 30 days so it is reviewed within the 45-day PMIERs certification window.
Present the ratio, the cushion, the stress projection and any breach of the internal cushion target.
Ask the committee to record either satisfaction with the sufficiency position or a specific instruction with an owner and a date.
Ensure the minutes state the actual ratio figure, not a general statement that capital was adequate.
checklist.done: each quarter's minutes record the actual sufficiency ratio, the cushion and either satisfaction or a dated instruction.

checklist.step: Keep the Section 506 internal audit reporting line intact
actions: Have the Audit Committee approve the internal audit charter, the annual plan and the budget by resolution, and minute the approval.
Hold a closed session with the committee at least annually with no management present and minute that it occurred.
Report the plan completion percentage and any management-driven scope reduction to the committee each quarter.
Have the committee, not management, approve the Chief Audit Executive's appointment, removal and remuneration, and record that in the minutes.
checklist.done: the charter, plan and budget are committee-approved by resolution and the closed session and appointment authority are minuted.

checklist.step: Run meetings so the record is examinable
actions: Issue the agenda and pack at least five business days before each meeting and record the distribution date in the portal.
Record attendance, apologies and quorum at the start of each set of minutes, and abandon or adjourn any meeting that opens without quorum rather than proceeding.
Minute the paper considered, the discussion, the decision, any dissent and the resolution wording for each item.
Circulate draft minutes within 10 business days and obtain chair approval at the following meeting.
checklist.done: every meeting has a dated pack distribution, a quorum record, decision-level minutes and chair-approved final minutes.

checklist.step: Track delegated authority and escalation triggers
actions: Maintain a register of every authority delegated by the board — investment limits, capital actions, reinsurance and risk transfer approvals — with the holder and the limit.
Log each exercise of a delegated authority with the date, the amount and the approver, and reconcile the register monthly to the transactions actually executed.
Flag any transaction executed above a delegated limit for board ratification at the next meeting.
Report exercises and breaches to the risk committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every delegated authority is registered and every exercise reconciled, with over-limit transactions routed for board ratification.

checklist.step: Escalate a shortfall or projected shortfall through the chartered path
actions: On identification that Available Assets are below, or projected below, Minimum Required Assets, convene the risk committee within 10 business days.
Present the shortfall amount, the cause, the remediation options — capital contribution, risk transfer, restricted new insurance written — and the recommended plan.
Obtain a board resolution on the plan and record that the Enterprises will be notified within 30 calendar days of identification.
Report progress against the plan at every subsequent board meeting until the ratio is restored.
checklist.done: any actual or projected shortfall reaches the risk committee within 10 business days and a board-resolved plan is minuted with the Enterprise notification date.

checklist.step: Review board and committee effectiveness annually
actions: Run an annual effectiveness questionnaire covering whether members receive the sufficiency pack in time and in a form they can challenge.
Assess attendance: any director below 75% attendance is discussed by the chair and the discussion is recorded.
Assess whether the committee had the information needed at each PMIERs decision point and record where it did not.
Produce an action list with owners and dates and report progress at the next annual review.
checklist.done: the annual effectiveness review is completed with an attendance analysis and an owned, dated action list.

checklist.step: Induct and train directors on the PMIERs financial requirements
actions: Give every new director an induction pack covering the PMIERs structure, the Available Assets and MRA computation, and the consequence of a shortfall for approved insurer status.
Assign the annual PMIERs refresher in the learning management system to all directors and committee members and track completion.
Run a session on the 2024 Available Asset amendment and its phase-in to September 30, 2026 before the first quarter in which a new phase-in step applies.
Record attendance and completion as governance evidence.
checklist.done: every director has completed induction and the annual PMIERs refresher, with amendment training delivered ahead of each phase-in step.

checklist.step: Reconcile the governance record to the corporate registers
actions: Reconcile the composition schedule to the statutory register of directors and to the filings made with the domiciliary insurance department.
Confirm every appointment and resignation has a signed consent or resignation letter on file with the effective date.
Confirm officer appointments approved by the board match the officer list used in regulatory filings and in the PMIERs certification signature block.
Correct any difference within 10 business days and record the correction.
checklist.done: the composition schedule, statutory registers and regulatory filings agree, with every appointment supported by a signed document.

checklist.step: Refresh charters when PMIERs or the governance rules change
actions: Log each PMIERs amendment and each domiciliary governance rule change in the Internal Regulatory System with its effective date.
Assess which charter clauses and which committee reporting requirements are affected and prepare the redline.
Table the redlined charter at the next committee and board meeting rather than waiting for the annual review.
Record the approval and the effective date and archive the superseded version.
checklist.done: each relevant change produces a redlined charter approved at the next meeting, with the superseded version archived.

checklist.step: Retain the governance record for examination
actions: Archive charters, composition schedules, packs, minutes and resolutions to the repository indexed by committee and meeting date.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the meeting date and confirm minutes cannot be edited after chair approval.
Confirm the four quarterly sufficiency minutes for each year can be produced as a single bundle on request.
Test retrieval annually by requesting the prior year's risk committee bundle.
checklist.done: the governance record is archived immutably, retention-labelled and retrievable as a per-year sufficiency bundle.

checklist.step: Report the governance position into the annual PMIERs package
actions: Prepare the annual governance summary: committee structure, charter approval dates, composition and independence, attendance and the four quarterly sufficiency reviews with their ratios.
Have the Board Governance Lead review and the board chair sign the summary.
Hand it to the Controller for inclusion in the package delivered to the Enterprises by April 15.
File the signed summary with the year's governance record.
checklist.done: a chair-signed annual governance summary listing the four quarterly sufficiency reviews is included in the April 15 package.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings, charters and sufficiency packs
actions: Export every board and committee meeting in the period with date, attendees, pack distribution date and minute status.
Export every charter in force with its approval date and version.
Add the four quarterly capital sufficiency packs and any shortfall escalation record, and reconcile the meeting count to the frequency each charter requires.
testing.done: the meeting, charter and pack population is exported and the meeting count reconciles to the charter-required frequency.

testing.step: Reconcile the charters to the PMIERs obligations
actions: Read Sections 701, 703 and 506 and list the oversight obligations each imposes on the board.
Match each obligation to a clause in a current charter and list any obligation with no charter clause.
Confirm each charter in force at each meeting date was the version the committee actually operated under, using the approval dates.
testing.done: every cited-section oversight obligation maps to a charter clause in force at the relevant meeting dates.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of meetings and decisions
actions: Take 100% of the quarterly risk committee meetings that considered capital sufficiency and 100% of shortfall escalations.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 other board or committee decisions from the period.
Record the seed, the population and the draw date so the reviewer can reproduce the sample.
testing.done: all sufficiency meetings and escalations are covered plus a reproducible sample of other decisions.

testing.step: Re-perform the quarterly sufficiency review from the minutes
actions: For each quarter, read the minutes and extract the sufficiency ratio and cushion actually recorded.
Compare those figures to the certified figures in the PMIERs certification package for the same quarter-end.
Confirm the projection presented used the phase-in percentage in force for the projected periods through September 30, 2026.
Treat a quarter whose minutes record no ratio figure as a fail even if a pack was distributed.
testing.done: each quarter's minuted ratio agrees to the certified figure and the projection used the correct phase-in percentages.

testing.step: Test composition, independence and quorum
actions: Rebuild the composition schedule from board resolutions and consent letters rather than from the maintained schedule.
Re-apply the independence criteria to each director using the questionnaire responses and the related party register, and list any determination you would have reached differently.
For each sampled meeting, recompute quorum from the attendance record against the charter requirement.
Confirm the Audit Committee financial expert designation is supported by the individual's recorded experience.
testing.done: composition is rebuilt from primary documents, independence is re-determined, and quorum is recomputed for every sampled meeting.

testing.step: Trace decisions to authority and to execution
actions: For each sampled decision, confirm the deciding body held the authority under the charter or the delegation register at that date.
Trace capital, investment and risk transfer decisions through to the executed transaction and confirm the amount matches the authority.
List any transaction executed above a delegated limit and confirm it was ratified at the next board meeting.
testing.done: every sampled decision sits within a charted or delegated authority and executed amounts match, with over-limit items ratified.

testing.step: Recompute the reporting and escalation clocks
actions: Compute quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and compare it to the date the risk committee minuted the sufficiency review for that quarter.
Compute pack distribution date plus five business days against each meeting date and list every late pack.
For any shortfall, compute identification date plus 10 business days to the committee meeting and plus 30 calendar days to the Enterprise notification and compare both to the record.
testing.done: every reporting and escalation clock is recomputed against the record with each breach listed.

testing.step: Test the internal audit reporting line in practice
actions: Confirm the Audit Committee approved the internal audit charter, plan and budget by minuted resolution in the period.
Confirm the annual closed session without management is minuted.
Test whether any plan item covering underwriting, quality control, claims or PMIERs reporting was descoped, and whether the descoping was reported to the committee.
testing.done: the charter, plan and budget approvals, the closed session and any descoping are all evidenced in the minutes.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the meeting or charter affected and the PMIERs oversight obligation left unmet.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — pack late, ratio not minuted, charter not updated, quorum failure, authority exceeded, vacancy unfilled — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a decision was taken without authority, require board ratification before closure.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's committee agenda.
testing.done: each exception has a root-caused, owned issue with a remediation date and, where needed, a ratification gate.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance thresholds on unminuted quarterly sufficiency reviews, uncharted committee action, quorum failures and late shortfall escalation.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the minutes relied on.
Have an Internal Auditor who neither drafts board papers nor takes minutes sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and, where governance exceptions exist, to the full board, and archive the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the stated thresholds and has been reported at committee and, where required, board level.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual plus event-driven; the annual filings are tested once after the June 1 CGAD date and the event-driven population is tested quarterly against the affiliate transaction and board change logs

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Compliance Officer outside the corporate secretariat who prepared or reviewed none of the sampled filings

Evidence location for test results.value: Governance disclosure test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository — obligation register extract, filing trace, exhibit completeness check and deadline recomputation — cross-linked from the Internal Regulatory System

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed disclosures with exhibits, submission receipts and the correspondence file, producible to the lead state, FHFA or the Enterprises within 5 business days
