checklist.step: Build the obligation register of governance and holding-company filings
actions: List every state where the approved insurer is domiciled or commercially domiciled and record which holding company act provisions each has adopted.

Create an obligation row per filing type per state: Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure, Form B registration statement, Form C summary, Form F enterprise risk report, Form D prior notice, Form A change of control.
Record each row's due date rule in words — for example CGAD by June 1 to the lead state, Form B within 120 days of fiscal year end — and the submission channel the department requires.
Name the lead state for CGAD purposes and record the basis for that determination.
Have the General Counsel confirm the register is complete before the calendar is generated from it.
checklist.done: the register holds one row per filing type per state with a stated due-date rule, submission channel and a confirmed lead state.

checklist.step: Generate the filing calendar and assign owners
actions: Generate dated calendar entries for the coming year from the obligation register and assign a preparer and a reviewer to each.
Set reminders at 90, 45 and 15 days before each annual due date and escalate to the General Counsel on any entry still unstarted at 15 days.
Add an event-driven watch list for affiliate transactions, board and senior officer changes, and any ownership movement approaching 10% of voting securities.
Publish the calendar to Legal, Finance and the secretariat and obtain each owner's acceptance.
checklist.done: every register row has a dated, owned, accepted calendar entry with escalation reminders and an event-driven watch list.

checklist.step: Draft the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure
actions: Draft the CGAD covering the level at which governance occurs, board and committee structure, director qualification and nomination process, board and management responsibilities, and executive compensation policies.
Source each factual statement from the board portal — charters, composition schedule, minutes, compensation committee resolutions — and footnote the source in the working draft.
State how the board oversees the PMIERs financial requirements, naming the risk committee's quarterly sufficiency review, since this is the governance the Enterprises rely on.
Compare the draft to last year's filed CGAD and list every change so the department can see what moved.
checklist.done: the CGAD draft covers every required content area with each statement sourced to a governance document and a change list against the prior year.

checklist.step: Prepare the holding-company registration statement and exhibits
actions: Update the organisational chart showing every entity in the insurance holding company system with ownership percentages and jurisdictions.
Schedule every affiliate agreement in force — management, service, tax sharing, cost allocation, reinsurance — with its effective date and the Form D notice reference under which it was approved.
List the ultimate controlling person and every person holding 10% or more of voting securities, reconciled to the share register.
Attach the audited financial statements and the Form F enterprise risk report addressing material risks in the holding company system that could affect the insurer.
checklist.done: the registration statement carries a current organisational chart, a complete affiliate agreement schedule tied to Form D references, and the required exhibits.

checklist.step: Legal review and officer certification of each filing
actions: Review each draft against the state's adopted form instructions clause by clause and mark any required item not answered.
Check consistency across filings — the CGAD, registration statement and audited statements must not describe the governance structure or the affiliate agreements differently.
Obtain the certifying officer's signature, confirming the officer named is currently appointed per the board minutes.
Record the review completion date at least 15 days before the due date so a rejection can be corrected in time.
checklist.done: each filing is clause-checked, cross-consistent, signed by a currently appointed officer and cleared at least 15 days before its due date.

checklist.step: Submit each filing through the channel the department requires
actions: Submit through the channel recorded on the obligation row — department electronic filing portal, secure email to the named analyst, or paper where the state still requires it.
Capture the submission receipt, confirmation number or delivery confirmation and attach it to the calendar entry the same day.
Where a filing fee applies, pay it by the department's accepted method and attach the payment confirmation.
Mark the calendar entry complete only when the receipt is attached, never on the act of sending.
checklist.done: every filing has a dated receipt attached to its calendar entry and no entry is closed without one.

checklist.step: Run the Form D prior-notice gate on affiliate transactions
actions: Block execution in the contract lifecycle system for any agreement where a counterparty is an affiliate of the approved insurer, routing it to the Form D gate.

Assess whether the transaction meets the state's prior-notice threshold — management or service agreements, cost sharing, tax allocation, reinsurance, guarantees, or transfers above the statutory percentage of surplus.
File the Form D at least 30 days before the proposed effective date and record the date the waiting period expires.
Release the contract for signature only after the waiting period expires without disapproval, or on written non-objection, and record which applied.
checklist.done: no affiliate agreement executes before its Form D waiting period expires, with the expiry or non-objection recorded per transaction.

checklist.step: Run the change-of-control gate
actions: Monitor the share register and any transaction discussions for a person acquiring 10% or more of voting securities, which presumes control.
Where the presumption arises, prepare the Form A statement with the acquiring person's biographical affidavits, financing plan and three-year business plan for the insurer.
File and obtain the commissioner's approval, including any public hearing, before the transaction closes — closing before approval is not curable.
Notify Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac of the proposed change of control, since approved insurer status depends on it, and record their responses.
checklist.done: any 10% acquisition is filed on Form A and approved before closing, with both Enterprises notified and their responses recorded.

checklist.step: Notify the Enterprises of governance and control changes
actions: Maintain a trigger list: change of control, change of ultimate controlling person, appointment or departure of the chief executive, chief financial or chief risk officer, and material changes to the committee structure overseeing PMIERs compliance.
On any trigger, prepare the notification stating the change, its effective date and the effect on PMIERs oversight, and have General Counsel clear it.
Send to both Enterprise relationship managers within 30 calendar days of the change taking effect and capture both acknowledgements.
Record the notification against the governance change in the board portal so the two records cannot drift.
checklist.done: every triggering change is notified to both Enterprises within 30 calendar days on cleared wording, with acknowledgements filed.

checklist.step: Handle department comments and amendments
actions: Log every department comment letter or information request against the filing with the response due date.
Draft the response, obtain General Counsel review, and file within the department's stated period, requesting an extension in writing before the date if more time is needed.
Where facts change after filing — a director resigns, an affiliate agreement is amended — file an amendment rather than waiting for next year's filing.
Record the resolution of each comment and close the tracker item only when the department confirms.
checklist.done: every comment has a filed response inside its period and every post-filing fact change has an amendment on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the disclosed facts to the source records quarterly
actions: Each quarter compare the filed organisational chart to the entity register and the filed director and officer lists to the board minutes.
Compare the affiliate agreement schedule to the contract lifecycle system inventory and investigate agreements present in one and absent from the other.
Compare the disclosed 10% holders to the current share register.
Raise a correction task for every difference with a decision on whether an amendment filing is required.
checklist.done: each quarter's reconciliation of chart, officers, affiliate agreements and holders is complete with amendment decisions recorded.

checklist.step: Coordinate with the lead state on the CGAD
actions: Confirm the lead state designation each year before filing, since it moves with the group's premium and domicile profile.
Confirm with the lead state analyst whether the CGAD is required as a standalone filing or by reference to the prior year where nothing changed.
Where filing by reference, file the statement of no material change with the specific prior-year filing referenced and its date.
Log the analyst's confirmation in the obligation register so the following year's approach is evidenced.
checklist.done: the lead state is confirmed for the year and the CGAD is filed in the form that state requires, with the confirmation logged.

checklist.step: Report the filing position to the board
actions: Table an annual filing status report showing every governance and holding-company filing due, filed and outstanding, with dates.
Report every late filing, every department comment and every Enterprise notification made in the year.
Ask the board to note the CGAD content before it is filed, since it describes the board's own governance.
Minute the board's noting and any direction given.
checklist.done: the board has noted the CGAD content and the annual filing status, with late filings and comments minuted.

checklist.step: Archive filings and receipts for examination
actions: Archive each filed document with its exhibits, the submission receipt and the correspondence file, indexed by state, filing type and year.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the filing date.
Confirm a single state's full file — CGAD, registration statement, Form D notices and correspondence — can be produced as one bundle.
Test retrieval annually by producing the prior year's lead state bundle.
checklist.done: filings, exhibits and receipts are archived, retention-labelled and producible as a single per-state bundle.

checklist.step: Refresh the register when a state amends its holding company act
actions: Monitor NAIC model law adoptions and state bulletins for changes to CGAD, Form B, Form D and Form F requirements and log each with its effective date.
Update the affected obligation rows — due date rule, content requirement, submission channel — and regenerate the calendar entries.
Assess whether any change requires an out-of-cycle filing or an amendment to a filing already made.
Brief the preparers and reviewers on the change before the next filing is drafted.
checklist.done: each statutory change is logged, the obligation register and calendar are regenerated, and preparers are briefed before the next draft.

testing.step: Build the population of due and completed filings
actions: Extract every obligation row with its due date, owner, filing status and receipt reference for the period.
Add the affiliate transaction log from the contract lifecycle system and the board and senior officer change log from the board portal so event-driven obligations are captured.
Reconcile the population to the states where the insurer is domiciled or commercially domiciled and explain any state with no obligation rows.
testing.done: the population covers annual and event-driven obligations across every relevant state and reconciles to the licensing footprint.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the statutes actually in force
actions: For the lead state and three other states, read the adopted holding company act and confirm the register's due-date rule and content requirements match it.
Confirm the CGAD lead state determination is correct for the year on the group's current profile.
List any obligation the statute imposes that the register omits as a coverage gap, not a documentation issue.
testing.done: the register's rules are confirmed against the statutes for the tested states and every omitted obligation is listed as a gap.

testing.step: Draw and document the filing sample
actions: Take 100% of annual filings — CGAD, Form B, Form F — and 100% of Form A filings in the period.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 Form D notices and 10 Enterprise notifications.
Record the seed, population sizes and draw date so the reviewer can reproduce the sample.
testing.done: all annual and change-of-control filings are covered plus a reproducible sample of Form D notices and Enterprise notifications.

testing.step: Re-perform the content completeness check
actions: Take the state's form instructions and work through each required item against the filed document, marking answered, partially answered or omitted.
For the CGAD, confirm it describes the board's oversight of the PMIERs financial requirements and names the committee performing it.
For the registration statement, confirm every affiliate agreement in the contract inventory appears on the schedule with a Form D reference.
List every omitted or partial item with the instruction clause it fails.
testing.done: each sampled filing is item-by-item complete against the instructions, or every omission is listed with its clause.

testing.step: Trace disclosed facts to the source records
actions: Trace the filed director and officer list to the board minutes appointing each and to any resignation letters.
Trace the organisational chart to the entity register and the 10% holder list to the share register at the filing date.
Trace the executive compensation description to the compensation committee resolutions.
List every disclosed fact that the source record does not support.
testing.done: every sampled disclosed fact traces to a dated source record, with unsupported statements listed.

testing.step: Recompute every due date and waiting period
actions: Recompute the CGAD due date as June 1 to the lead state and the Form B due date from fiscal year end plus the state's period, and compare to the receipt dates.
For each sampled Form D, compute filing date plus 30 days and compare it to the agreement's execution date.
For each Enterprise notification, compute the change effective date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the acknowledgement date.
Treat any execution inside a waiting period or any receipt after a due date as a fail with no materiality argument.
testing.done: every due date and waiting period is recomputed against the actual receipt or execution date, with breaches recorded as fails.

testing.step: Verify the change-of-control gate held
actions: Review share register movements in the period for any person crossing 10% of voting securities.
For each, confirm a Form A was filed and the commissioner's approval order pre-dates the closing date.
Confirm both Enterprises were notified and that their responses on continued approved insurer status are on file.
Treat any closing before approval as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every control acquisition has an approval order pre-dating closing and Enterprise responses on file.

testing.step: Test the quarterly reconciliation control
actions: Confirm a completed reconciliation exists for each quarter comparing chart, officers, affiliate agreements and 10% holders to source.
Re-perform one quarter's reconciliation independently and compare your differences to the differences recorded.
Confirm each recorded difference has an amendment decision, and that decisions to not amend carry a written rationale.
testing.done: all four quarterly reconciliations exist, one re-performs successfully, and every difference has a reasoned amendment decision.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the state, filing type, the requirement missed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — register omission, calendar not regenerated after a statutory change, contract gate bypassed, trigger not recognised, receipt never obtained — and an owner.
Set a remediation date, requiring an amended or late filing to be made within 30 calendar days with General Counsel sign-off.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's event-driven test.
testing.done: each exception has a root-caused, owned issue with a 30-day corrective filing commitment and General Counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance thresholds on missed annual dates, waiting-period breaches, unapproved control changes and unnotified governance changes.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the recomputed dates and instruction-clause checks behind it.
Have a Compliance Officer who prepared or reviewed none of the sampled filings sign the workpaper.
Report to the governance committee and the Audit Committee via the board portal and archive the workpaper with the year's filing record.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the zero-tolerance thresholds and has been reported at committee level and archived.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief HR Officer owns the fitness-and-propriety assessment process for officers and directors of the approved insurer; General Counsel owns the disqualification determination and the regulator and Enterprise notifications

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the PMIERs 2024 Available Asset amendment and Sections 402 and 600-601 for the competence expected of the officers running property valuation and lender approval, read with the domiciliary state's officer and director biographical affidavit requirement and the federal prohibition on employing persons convicted of dishonesty offences without a written waiver

In-scope processes.value: Appointment, re-appointment and annual re-assessment of directors, executive officers and the senior individuals accountable for underwriting, quality control, claims, property valuation and lender approval and monitoring at the approved insurer

In-scope systems.value: Position and appointment records in Workday HCM; biographical affidavits, background reports and disqualification determinations held in the legal document repository and linked from the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Officer and Director Fitness and Propriety Procedure — covered-role schedule, biographical affidavit and third-party verification, background and sanctions screening, competence assessment against the role, disqualification determination, annual re-attestation and the notification path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief HR Officer and the General Counsel and endorsed by the board's governance committee; reviewed annually and on any change to state biographical affidavit requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Assessment completed and signed before the appointment effective date; biographical affidavit verification no older than three years at appointment; regulator notification of officer and director changes within the domiciliary period, commonly 30 days; Enterprise notification of senior officer changes within 30 calendar days; annual re-attestation completed by April 15 to support the annual PMIERs package

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workday triggers the assessment task the day an offer or nomination is recorded and blocks the appointment effective date until it closes; a 30-day post-appointment reminder drives the regulator and Enterprise notifications; an annual campaign opens each January with an April 15 cut-off

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Biographical affidavits, third-party verification reports, screening results, competence assessments, disqualification determinations and annual attestations retained 7 years from the individual's departure, under restricted access

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments made before assessment completion, expired verifications, unreturned attestations and undisclosed matters found later are each logged with the reassessment outcome and any restriction placed on the role

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs every disqualification or fit-with-conditions determination and clears any waiver application or regulator notification

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment, re-appointment and role change into a covered position in the period, plus the full covered-population annual re-attestation cycle

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one appointment effective before a signed assessment, one covered individual with no current verified biographical affidavit, or one unreturned annual attestation at April 15 fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per appointment with an annual re-assessment; new appointments are tested quarterly and the full covered population is tested annually after the April 15 attestation cut-off

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Compliance Officer outside HR and Legal who performed none of the sampled assessments and holds no line responsibility for the covered roles

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual fitness and propriety test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access, holding the covered-role reconciliation, sample, re-performed screenings and the attestation completeness analysis

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Covered-role schedule, biographical affidavits with verification reports, screening summaries and determinations, producible to the domiciliary department, FHFA or the Enterprises within 10 business days under a confidentiality cover

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel responds to department and Enterprise questions on an individual's fitness; the Chief HR Officer supplies employment records; nothing about an individual leaves the company without General Counsel clearance

checklist.step: Define the covered-role schedule
actions: List every position requiring assessment: all directors, the chief executive, chief financial, chief risk and chief actuary roles, the chief audit executive, and the heads of underwriting, quality control, claims, property valuation and lender approval.
Justify each inclusion against PMIERs — Sections 600 and 601 make lender approval and monitoring a named accountability, and Section 402 makes property valuation one.
Tag each covered position in Workday HCM with a fitness-assessment flag so any requisition or internal move into it triggers the process automatically.
Review the schedule annually and on any reorganisation that moves a PMIERs accountability to a different position.
checklist.done: every covered position is listed with its PMIERs justification and flagged in Workday so appointments trigger the assessment.

checklist.step: Trigger the assessment at nomination or offer
actions: Open the fitness assessment case the day a candidate is nominated by the nominating committee or an offer is approved for a covered position.
Record the proposed appointment effective date and set the assessment completion gate at least 10 business days before it.

Notify the candidate what will be collected — biographical affidavit, identity and employment history, regulatory and criminal record checks, credit and sanctions screening — and obtain written consent.
Block the Workday appointment transaction from being effective until the case closes with a signed determination.
checklist.done: a case is open with consent captured and the appointment transaction is blocked until a signed determination exists.

checklist.step: Collect and verify the biographical affidavit
actions: Issue the NAIC-format biographical affidavit in DocuSign and require every question answered, refusing partially completed forms rather than chasing later.
Confirm the affidavit is notarised where the domiciliary state requires it and that the signature date is within the current appointment cycle.
Commission the third-party verification report from a service the department accepts, covering identity, education, employment history, regulatory actions and litigation.
Confirm the verification is no older than three years at the appointment date and re-commission where it is not.
checklist.done: a fully answered, correctly executed affidavit is on file with a third-party verification report less than three years old.

checklist.step: Run the regulatory, criminal and sanctions screening
actions: Screen the individual against criminal records for offences involving dishonesty or breach of trust, since employing such a person without a written waiver is prohibited.
Screen against state insurance department disciplinary and revocation actions, federal agency debarment and exclusion lists, and any FHFA or Enterprise suspended counterparty list.
Run sanctions and politically exposed person screening and clear every potential match with documented reasoning rather than closing on a name mismatch alone.
Record each search performed, the source, the date and the result, and attach the raw reports to the case.
checklist.done: every required screen is run and evidenced with its source and date, and every potential match is cleared with written reasoning.

checklist.step: Assess competence against the specific role
actions: Write the role's competence requirements before assessing the person — for the head of lender approval that means experience of counterparty approval, monitoring and termination under Sections 600 and 601.
Assess the individual's experience against each requirement using the affidavit, references and interview notes, marking met, partially met or not met.
Where a requirement is partially met, define the mitigation — a named deputy, a training plan with dates, or a time-limited restriction on the role.
Obtain two references covering the individual's conduct in a comparable role and record what each said.
checklist.done: the competence assessment marks each pre-written requirement met, partially met or not met, with mitigations and two recorded references.

checklist.step: Assess propriety, conflicts and financial soundness
actions: Review the individual's declared outside directorships, business interests and relationships with lenders, servicers, reinsurers and the audit firm for conflicts with the covered role.
Where a conflict exists, record the management measure — recusal from named decisions, divestment, or refusal of the appointment — and who monitors it.
Review the financial soundness indicators the domiciliary state requires, such as bankruptcies or unsatisfied judgements, and assess relevance to the role's financial accountabilities.
Enter the conflicts on the conflicts register with a review date.
checklist.done: conflicts and financial soundness matters are assessed, entered on the register with a monitor and a review date, or the appointment is refused.

checklist.step: Take and sign the determination
actions: Read the affidavit, verification, screening results, competence assessment and conflicts review together and record a determination of fit, fit with conditions, or not fit.
State the conditions explicitly where fit with conditions applies, with an owner and a review date for each.
Where a disqualifying conviction exists, determine whether a written waiver is required and obtainable before any appointment can proceed.
Sign and date the determination and release the Workday appointment block only on a fit or fit-with-conditions outcome.
checklist.done: a signed, dated determination exists before the appointment effective date, with any conditions owned and dated.

checklist.step: Take the appointment through the board
actions: Table the appointment with the determination summary — not the underlying personal data — at the nominating or governance committee and then the board.
Record the board resolution appointing the individual with the effective date and any conditions attached to the appointment.
Update the composition schedule, the statutory register of directors and officers and the officer list used in regulatory filings.
Confirm the individual has signed the code of conduct and the conflicts declaration before the effective date.
checklist.done: the appointment is resolved by the board with conditions minuted and the statutory registers and officer lists updated.

checklist.step: Notify the regulator and the Enterprises
actions: File the officer or director change with the domiciliary department in the form and period it requires, attaching the biographical affidavit where mandated.

Notify Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac of any change to the chief executive, chief financial, chief risk or chief actuary roles, or to the heads of underwriting, quality control, claims or lender approval, within 30 calendar days of effect.
Capture the department receipt and both Enterprise acknowledgements against the appointment record.
Where the Enterprises ask follow-up questions on the individual's experience, answer through General Counsel with the competence assessment as support.
checklist.done: the department filing and both Enterprise notifications are made within their periods with receipts filed against the appointment.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-attestation for the whole covered population
actions: Open the annual campaign each January to every covered individual asking whether any matter in their affidavit has changed — new directorships, regulatory action, criminal matter, litigation, bankruptcy or conflict.
Require a positive or negative answer to each question and reject blanket confirmations.
Chase weekly and escalate any non-response to the individual's manager at 30 days and to the Chief HR Officer at 45 days.
Close the campaign by April 15 so the result supports the annual PMIERs package.
checklist.done: every covered individual has answered each attestation question by April 15, with non-responses escalated and recorded.

checklist.step: Reassess on any disclosed or discovered change
actions: Open a reassessment within five business days of any positive attestation answer, adverse media hit, regulatory action or internal investigation involving a covered individual.
Re-run the affected screening and assess whether the determination changes, recording the reasoning either way.
Where fitness is impaired, decide on restriction, suspension from the covered accountability, or removal, and record who decided.
Notify the department and the Enterprises where the individual holds a PMIERs-named accountability and the outcome affects it.
checklist.done: each disclosed or discovered matter has a dated reassessment, a recorded decision and, where required, regulator and Enterprise notification.

checklist.step: Refresh verifications before they expire
actions: Maintain an expiry date per individual for the biographical affidavit verification and the criminal record check.
Generate a Workday task 90 days before expiry assigning the refresh to the individual and the case owner.
Re-commission the verification and re-run the screening, and treat an expired verification on a serving officer as an open exception until refreshed.
Update the expiry date on completion and archive the superseded report.
checklist.done: no covered individual serves with an expired verification, and refreshes start 90 days ahead of expiry.

checklist.step: Control access to the assessment record
actions: Restrict the fitness assessment repository to named HR, Legal and Compliance roles and remove standing access for everyone else.
Log and review access to individual files quarterly, investigating any access without a case reference.
Apply the 7-year-from-departure retention and confirm files are purged on schedule rather than retained indefinitely.
Confirm the lawful basis and the privacy notice given to candidates cover the screening actually performed.
checklist.done: access is role-restricted and reviewed quarterly, retention runs from departure, and the privacy notice matches the screening performed.

checklist.step: Report the population position to the governance committee
actions: Report annually the covered population count, assessments completed, conditions in force, reassessments opened and attestation completion rate.
Report every appointment that proceeded before its determination was signed as a named exception.
Ask the committee to confirm the covered-role schedule still reflects the PMIERs accountabilities after any reorganisation.
Minute the committee's confirmation and any direction.
checklist.done: the governance committee has received and minuted the annual fitness position including named exceptions and a schedule confirmation.

checklist.step: Feed the outcome into the annual PMIERs package
actions: Prepare the annual statement of covered-role fitness: population, completion rate, open conditions and any disqualification, without personal detail.
Have the General Counsel review it for privacy and accuracy before release.
Hand it to the Controller for the package delivered to the Enterprises by April 15.
File the statement with the year's governance evidence.
checklist.done: a General Counsel-reviewed annual fitness statement is included in the April 15 Enterprise package and filed.

testing.step: Build the population of covered individuals and appointments
actions: Extract every position flagged as covered in Workday with its current holder, appointment date and any prior holder in the period.
Add director appointments and resignations from the board minutes and the statutory register.
Reconcile the covered-position list to the current organisation chart and to the PMIERs accountability map, listing any accountability with no flagged position.
testing.done: the population covers every covered position and appointment and reconciles to the org chart and the PMIERs accountability map.

testing.step: Reconcile the covered-role schedule to the PMIERs accountabilities
actions: Read Sections 402, 600 and 601 and list the named operational accountabilities they create.
Match each to a covered position and its current holder, and mark any accountability held by an unassessed individual as a coverage gap.
Confirm any position added or removed from the schedule in the period was approved by the General Counsel with a recorded rationale.
testing.done: every PMIERs-named accountability sits with an assessed individual, and schedule changes carry a recorded rationale.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of appointments and role changes into covered positions in the period and 100% of fit-with-conditions determinations.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 serving covered individuals from the annual attestation population.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the draw date so the sample can be reproduced.
testing.done: all new appointments and conditional determinations are covered plus a reproducible sample of serving individuals.

testing.step: Re-perform the determination on sampled appointments
actions: Read the affidavit, verification report, screening results and competence assessment and reach your own fitness conclusion before opening the signed determination.
Check the competence requirements were written before the assessment, not reverse-engineered from the candidate's history.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded determination and list every difference, including a right conclusion reached on incomplete evidence.
Confirm each condition attached to a fit-with-conditions outcome has an owner, a review date and evidence it was monitored.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has an independent conclusion compared to the recorded determination, with conditions traced to monitoring evidence.

testing.step: Re-run the screening on a sub-sample
actions: For 10 sampled individuals, re-run the criminal, regulatory action, debarment and sanctions screens today and compare the hits to the file.
Investigate any hit that exists now but was not on the file at assessment, and establish whether it pre-dated the assessment.
Confirm every potential match on file was cleared with written reasoning rather than closed silently.
Confirm no covered individual appears on an Enterprise or FHFA suspended counterparty list.
testing.done: screens re-run for 10 individuals with every new or pre-existing hit investigated and no suspended-counterparty match.

testing.step: Test appointment sequencing against the determination date
actions: For each sampled appointment, compare the signed determination date to the appointment effective date in Workday and to the board resolution date.
Confirm the Workday block actually prevented an effective date before the determination, rather than being overridden.
List every appointment effective before a signed determination as a fail regardless of the eventual outcome.
testing.done: every appointment is proven effective only after a signed determination, with overrides listed as fails.

testing.step: Recompute verification currency and notification deadlines
actions: For each sampled individual, compute the age of the biographical affidavit verification at the appointment date and today, against the three-year currency rule.
For each covered appointment, compute effective date plus 30 calendar days and compare to the Enterprise acknowledgement dates and the department filing receipt.
Compare the annual attestation campaign close date to April 15 and list any individual outstanding at that date.
testing.done: verification currency and every notification and attestation deadline is recomputed with each breach listed.

testing.step: Test the reassessment trigger in practice
actions: List every positive attestation answer, adverse media alert and internal investigation involving a covered individual in the period.
Confirm a reassessment was opened within five business days of each and closed with a recorded decision.
Where a determination changed, confirm the restriction, suspension or removal was executed and the regulator and Enterprises notified where required.
testing.done: every trigger produced a reassessment inside five business days with a recorded decision and any required notification.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the position, the requirement missed and the PMIERs accountability exposed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — position not flagged, block overridden, verification lapsed, attestation not chased, trigger missed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date, requiring any missing assessment to be completed within 30 calendar days and the individual's accountability restricted until it is.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly appointment test.
testing.done: each exception has a root-caused, owned issue with a 30-day completion commitment and an interim restriction where fitness is unproven.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance thresholds on appointments before determination, expired verifications and unreturned April 15 attestations.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the sampled files, redacted of personal data.
Have a Compliance Officer outside HR and Legal who performed none of the sampled assessments sign the workpaper.
Report to the governance committee in closed session and archive the workpaper under restricted access.
testing.done: a signed, personal-data-redacted workpaper states the conclusion and has been reported in a minuted closed session.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Board Governance Lead owns the annual board approval cycle for the policies PMIERs requires the approved insurer to operate under; each policy has a named executive owner who drafts it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the FHFA/Enterprises 2024 Available Asset amendment drives the investment and capital policy content, PMIERs Section 402 drives the property valuation policy, and Sections 600-601 drive the lender approval and monitoring policy; each is re-read at the annual policy review

In-scope processes.value: Annual board review and approval of the capital management policy, investment policy statement, underwriting guidelines, quality control plan, property valuation policy, lender approval and monitoring policy, claims policy, internal audit charter, code of conduct and business continuity policy for the mortgage guaranty approved insurer

In-scope systems.value: Policy drafts, redlines, committee papers, board resolutions and the approved policy library held in the board portal, with the published versions distributed through the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Board Policy Approval Procedure — policy inventory with owners and review cycles, drafting and redline standard, committee routing, board resolution wording, publication and attestation, and the out-of-cycle amendment path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the governance committee's recommendation and reviewed annually alongside the policy inventory itself

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every in-scope policy approved at least annually with no policy exceeding 12 months since its last board approval; the amended Available Asset standard reflected in the investment and capital policies before each phase-in step and fully by September 30, 2026; approved policy set summarised in the annual PMIERs package by April 15

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal tasks fire 120, 90 and 45 days before each policy's approval anniversary to the policy owner, escalating to the Board Governance Lead at 45 days and to the board chair at 15 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved policy versions, redlines against the prior version, committee papers, board minutes and resolutions, and publication and attestation records retained 7 years from supersession

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Policies operated beyond their approval anniversary, policies changed without board approval, and unattested populations are each logged with the ratification or re-approval date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Board Governance Lead signs off closure of policy-cycle exceptions; the board ratifies by resolution any policy that operated past its anniversary

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every policy on the in-scope inventory, each version approved in the period, the corresponding board resolutions, and the publication and attestation records for each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one in-scope policy operating more than 12 months since board approval, one substantive change made without board approval, or one policy whose content contradicts a current PMIERs requirement fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual; the full inventory is tested once a year after the last scheduled approval, with a quarterly ageing check that no policy is drifting past its anniversary

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Auditor who drafted none of the sampled policies and holds no ownership of any in-scope policy

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository — inventory extract, approval-date recomputation, content-to-requirement mapping and attestation analysis — cross-linked from the board portal

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy inventory with approval dates, the approved policy set, board resolutions and the publication record, producible to FHFA, the Enterprises or the domiciliary examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary produces the policy set and resolutions; the relevant executive policy owner answers content questions with General Counsel clearing any response about a policy that was out of cycle

checklist.step: Maintain the in-scope policy inventory
actions: List every policy the board must approve for the approved insurer, naming for each the executive owner, the approving body, the last approval date and the next anniversary.

Map each policy to the PMIERs requirement it serves — investment and capital policies to the Available Asset standard and Section 701, property valuation policy to Section 402, lender approval and monitoring policy to Sections 600 and 601.
Mark any policy with no PMIERs mapping and no other regulatory driver for consolidation rather than carrying it through the cycle.
Have the governance committee confirm the inventory annually and minute the confirmation.
checklist.done: the inventory names owner, approver, last approval and next anniversary for every policy, each mapped to the requirement it serves.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual approval cycle across board meetings
actions: Spread the policies across the year's board and committee meetings so no single meeting carries more than four policy approvals.
Set each policy's paper deadline at 15 business days before its meeting and its draft-complete date 45 days before.
Load 120, 90 and 45-day reminders to each policy owner and escalate at 45 days to the Board Governance Lead.
Publish the cycle and obtain each owner's written acceptance of their dates.
checklist.done: every policy has a scheduled meeting, dated draft and paper deadlines, reminders and an owner who has accepted the dates.

checklist.step: Refresh the capital management and investment policies for the amended standard
actions: Rewrite the eligible-asset schedule in the investment policy statement to mirror the amended Available Asset standard's credit-quality and liquidity distinctions.
Write the residential-mortgage-backed and commercial-real-estate-backed asset limits into the policy as hard limits with internal warning levels set inside them.
State the internal PMIERs sufficiency cushion target above 1.00 and the actions triggered at each breach level, with the action owner named.
Include the phase-in schedule through September 30, 2026 so the policy remains correct at each step rather than needing a re-draft each quarter.
Have the Chief Investment Officer and Chief Risk Officer clear the draft before it goes to committee.
checklist.done: the investment and capital policies carry the amended eligible-asset schedule, hard limits, a cushion target with owned triggers and the phase-in schedule.

checklist.step: Refresh the property valuation policy for Section 402
actions: State which valuation types are acceptable for insurance eligibility — full appraisal, appraisal waiver, automated valuation — and the circumstances permitting each.
State the appraiser independence and the appraisal review requirements, including when a second valuation is required.
State the tolerance for value variance that triggers escalation and who resolves it.
Cross-reference the operating procedure that implements the policy so the board approves the principle and management owns the detail.
checklist.done: the property valuation policy states acceptable valuation types, independence and review rules and the variance escalation tolerance.

checklist.step: Refresh the lender approval and monitoring policy for Sections 600-601
actions: State the approval criteria for a lender counterparty — financial condition, quality control capability, delinquency and rescission history, and licensing.
State the ongoing monitoring cycle, the metrics monitored and the thresholds that trigger a formal review.
State the suspension and termination authorities, who exercises them and how the decision is documented.
State how monitoring outcomes feed the underwriting guidelines so a poor counterparty changes the risk accepted, not just the watchlist.
checklist.done: the lender policy states approval criteria, a monitoring cycle with thresholds, named suspension authorities and the feedback into underwriting.

checklist.step: Produce each policy paper with a redline and an impact statement
actions: Attach to every policy paper a redline against the currently approved version so the board approves the change, not a clean document.
Write an impact statement covering what changed, why, which PMIERs requirement or amendment drove it, and what the operational effect is.
State whether any current practice would breach the amended policy and what will change before the effective date.
Have the policy owner and General Counsel sign the paper before it is loaded to the portal.
checklist.done: every policy paper carries a redline, an impact statement naming the driving requirement, and owner and legal signatures.

checklist.step: Route each policy through its committee before the board
actions: Route capital and investment policies through the risk and investment committees, underwriting, valuation and lender policies through the risk committee, and the internal audit charter through the Audit Committee.
Minute the committee's recommendation to the board, including any amendment the committee requires.
Carry committee amendments into the draft before the board paper is issued rather than tabling them verbally at the board.
Confirm the committee had the current version in front of it by recording the version number in the minutes.
checklist.done: each policy carries a minuted committee recommendation on a version-numbered draft with committee amendments already incorporated.

checklist.step: Take the board approval and record the resolution
actions: Table each policy with its redline and impact statement and record a resolution naming the policy, the version number and the effective date.
Record any condition the board attaches — for example that a limit tightens once the next phase-in step applies — with an owner and a date.
Record dissent where expressed, since a policy carried over objection needs the objection visible at examination.
Confirm quorum at the meeting and that the approving body matches the inventory's stated approver.
checklist.done: every policy has a board resolution naming version and effective date, with conditions, dissent and quorum recorded.

checklist.step: Publish the approved version and withdraw the superseded one
actions: Publish the approved version to the policy library with the version number, board approval date and effective date on the cover page.
Withdraw the superseded version from circulation and archive it so no team can operate from a stale copy.
Notify every affected function of the change and the effective date, and confirm procedure owners have scheduled their procedure updates.
Confirm the library index shows current version and approval date for every in-scope policy.
checklist.done: the approved version is published with its approval and effective dates, the prior version is withdrawn, and affected functions are notified.

checklist.step: Cascade policy changes into procedures and system controls
actions: For each approved change, identify the procedures, system limits and control descriptions that must move, and raise a task per item with an owner and a date.
For investment policy limit changes, confirm the limit is coded as a pre-trade rule and produces a warning before quarter-end rather than after.
For underwriting and lender policy changes, confirm the underwriting workstation rules and the counterparty monitoring reports were updated.
Close each task only on evidence the change is live, not on the owner's confirmation.
checklist.done: every policy change has cascaded tasks closed on live evidence, including coded pre-trade limits and updated underwriting rules.

checklist.step: Run the policy attestation for affected staff
actions: Assign the approved policy and any accompanying training to the affected population in the learning management system with a 30-day completion window.
Require an attestation that the individual has read and will apply the policy, with the version number recorded in the attestation.
Chase non-completions weekly and escalate to the function head at 30 days.
Report completion rates by function to the Board Governance Lead.
checklist.done: the affected population has attested to the version-numbered policy within 30 days, with non-completions escalated and rates reported.

checklist.step: Handle out-of-cycle amendments
actions: Where a PMIERs amendment or Enterprise letter makes a policy wrong, prepare the amendment for the next scheduled meeting rather than waiting for the anniversary.
Where the change cannot wait, use the written resolution procedure in the articles and record the circulated resolution with each director's signature.
Ratify every written resolution at the next full meeting and minute the ratification.
Record the out-of-cycle change on the inventory so the next anniversary is measured from it.
checklist.done: urgent changes are made by minuted written resolution and ratified at the next meeting, with the inventory anniversary reset.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly ageing check on the inventory
actions: Each quarter compute months elapsed since last board approval for every in-scope policy and list anything past 10 months as at risk.
Escalate anything past 12 months to the board chair the same week as an operating-without-approval exception.
Confirm the inventory's next-anniversary dates still match the scheduled meeting dates after any meeting is moved.
Report the ageing to the governance committee each quarter.
checklist.done: the quarterly ageing report lists at-risk and overdue policies and has been reported to the governance committee.

checklist.step: Report the approved policy set into the annual PMIERs package
actions: Prepare the annual policy schedule listing each in-scope policy, its version, board approval date and the PMIERs requirement it serves.
Attach the capital management, investment, property valuation and lender approval policies where the Enterprises request the documents themselves.
Have the Board Governance Lead review and the board chair sign the schedule.
Hand it to the Controller for the package delivered by April 15 and file the signed schedule.
checklist.done: a chair-signed policy schedule with approval dates and PMIERs mappings is included in the April 15 package.

checklist.step: Archive the policy governance record
actions: Archive each approved version with its redline, impact statement, committee minute, board resolution and publication record, indexed by policy and version.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the date the version was superseded.
Confirm a full approval history for a single policy can be produced as one chronological bundle.
Test retrieval annually on the investment policy statement, since it is the one examiners ask for first.
checklist.done: every version is archived with its full approval trail, retention-labelled and retrievable as a chronological per-policy bundle.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope policies and approvals
actions: Extract the policy inventory with owner, approving body, last approval date, version and next anniversary.
Extract every board and committee resolution in the period that approved a policy, with the version number named in the resolution.
Reconcile the two: every inventory entry must have a resolution and every resolution must match an inventory entry, and explain each difference.
testing.done: the inventory and the resolution list reconcile in both directions with every difference explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to the PMIERs requirements
actions: List the requirements imposed by the 2024 Available Asset amendment and by Sections 402 and 600-601.
Match each to an in-scope policy that governs it, and mark any requirement governed only by a management-level procedure as a coverage gap.
Confirm the inventory itself was confirmed by the governance committee in the period with the confirmation minuted.
testing.done: every cited requirement is governed by a board-approved policy or listed as a gap, and the inventory confirmation is minuted.

testing.step: Draw and document the policy sample
actions: Take 100% of the capital management policy, investment policy statement, property valuation policy and lender approval and monitoring policy.
Take a seeded random sample of six other in-scope policies approved in the period.
Record the seed, the inventory size and the draw date so the reviewer can reproduce the sample.
testing.done: all PMIERs-critical policies are covered plus a reproducible random sample of the remainder.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check against the requirement
actions: Read the amended Available Asset standard and check the investment policy's eligible-asset schedule reproduces its credit-quality and liquidity distinctions and its RMBS and CRE limits.
Check the property valuation policy against Section 402 for acceptable valuation types, appraiser independence and review requirements.
Check the lender policy against Sections 600 and 601 for approval criteria, monitoring cycle and termination authority.
List every requirement the policy text does not cover or covers in terms that contradict the requirement.
testing.done: each PMIERs-critical policy is read clause by clause against its requirement with gaps and contradictions listed.

testing.step: Trace each approval to a valid resolution
actions: For each sampled policy, open the board minute and confirm the resolution names the policy, the version and the effective date.
Confirm quorum was recorded and that the approving body matches the inventory's stated approver.
Confirm the committee recommendation pre-dates the board resolution and that committee amendments appear in the approved version.
Confirm the version approved is the version published in the policy library.
testing.done: each approval traces to a quorate resolution naming the published version, with committee amendments carried through.

testing.step: Recompute approval ageing across the inventory
actions: Compute months elapsed from last board approval to the period end for every in-scope policy.
List every policy over 12 months as an automatic fail and every policy over 10 months as an at-risk item.
Confirm any policy that passed 12 months was ratified by a later board resolution and that the ratification is minuted.
Confirm out-of-cycle written resolutions were ratified at the following full meeting.
testing.done: ageing is recomputed for every policy, overdue policies are listed as fails and every ratification is traced to a minute.

testing.step: Test that approved changes reached the operating environment
actions: For the investment policy, confirm each hard limit and internal warning level is coded in Aladdin compliance and produces a pre-trade warning, by inspecting the rule configuration.
For the lender policy, confirm the monitoring report includes every metric and threshold the policy names.
For the property valuation policy, confirm the underwriting workstation enforces the second-valuation trigger at the stated variance tolerance.
Treat a policy change that never reached the system as a fail even where the policy itself was approved on time.
testing.done: each sampled policy change is proven live in the system it governs, with unimplemented changes recorded as fails.

testing.step: Test publication and attestation
actions: Confirm the published version in the policy library matches the approved version number and that the superseded version is withdrawn.
Extract the attestation completion rate per policy and compare it to the affected population defined at assignment.
Sample five attestations and confirm the version number attested matches the approved version.
List any population with completion below 100% at the 30-day window close.
testing.done: published versions match approvals, superseded versions are withdrawn, and attestation completeness is measured against the defined population.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the policy, the PMIERs requirement affected and whether the company operated without a valid approved policy.
Assign a root cause from the fixed set — meeting moved without rescheduling, owner missed the draft date, redline not produced, change never cascaded, attestation not chased — and an owner.
Set a remediation date requiring re-approval or ratification at the next meeting, and require the Board Governance Lead's sign-off before closure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly ageing report.
testing.done: each exception has a root-caused, owned issue with a re-approval or ratification commitment and a Board Governance Lead sign-off gate.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Apply the zero-tolerance thresholds on policies past 12 months, unapproved substantive changes and policy text contradicting a current PMIERs requirement.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the ageing recomputation and the clause-by-clause content check behind it.
Have an Internal Auditor who owns and drafted none of the in-scope policies sign the workpaper.
Report to the governance committee and the board via the board portal and archive the workpaper with the year's governance record.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion against the stated thresholds and has been reported to the governance committee and the board.
